title: Diamondbacks news: Kevin Ginkel drops 'disappointing' reaction to Ketel Marte's recent absence
description: Kevin Ginkel didn’t hide his frustration when asked about Ketel Marte’s recent absence , offering a candid take on a situation that has rattled the Arizona Diamondbacks clubhouse during a critical stretch of the season. The veteran reliever made clear how much the team needs its star second baseman back. “For us to go where we want to go, we’ve got […] The post Diamondbacks news: Kevin Ginkel drops 'disappointing' reaction to Ketel Marte's recent absence appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Diamondbacks news: Kevin Ginkel drops 'disappointing' reaction to Ketel Marte's recent absence appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Kevin Ginkel didn't hide his frustration when asked about Ketel Marte's recent absence, offering a candid take on a situation that has rattled the Arizona Diamondbacks clubhouse during a critical stretch of the season.

The veteran reliever made clear how much the team needs its star second baseman back. "For us to go where we want to go, we've got to have them here," Ginkel said. "It's disappointing how the things that happened happened. There's really no explanation for it."

"It's disappointing… there's really no explanation for it."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Kevin Ginkel on Ketel Marte's recent absence 😳 pic.twitter.com/IW4IIU8o1M

— PHNX Diamondbacks (@PHNX_Dbacks) August 21, 2026

The comments come amid one of the stranger chapters of Arizona's season. Marte failed to show up for the Diamondbacks' game against the Boston Red Sox on Aug. 17, prompting the team to place the three-time All-Star on the restricted list. Manager Torey Lovullo admitted he felt "betrayed" once the situation unfolded, though he said he had since moved past that initial frustration.

Ginkel, who has been Marte's teammate since 2019, acknowledged that the abrupt nature of the disappearance stung throughout the room.

"I think a lot of players are kind of frustrated with how it just happened," he said. Still, he emphasized his care for Marte, stressing that the priority is getting him healthy both physically and mentally so he can return and contribute.

Several players are hoping for clarity. Asked whether he expected an explanation, Ginkel said it would be nice to hear one. Lovullo, for his part, met with Marte, general manager Mike Hazen, and Marte's agent on Thursday, describing a conversation in which both sides got what they needed off their chests.

The backdrop makes the drama especially costly. Arizona entered Friday with 34 games remaining, locked in a tight playoff race and chasing its first postseason berth since 2023. Marte was eventually moved from the restricted list to the 10-day injured list, with reports pointing to inflammation in his knee and upper hamstring.

For Ginkel and the Diamondbacks, the focus now is on channeling the noise into a push. As he put it, the hope is to get Marte back and let the team make a run at October.

title: Seven things we've learned ahead of Town's Premier League return
description: Blues chairman Mark Ashton on digital ticketing, the new manager, training ground and more.
fullText:
Ipswich Town take to the pitch at Portman Road at 15:00 BST for their first game back in the Premier League. Following a busy summer of transfers and the appointment of new manager Gary O'Neil, club chairman Mark Ashton told the BBC he was "optimistic" ahead of the clash against Sunderland. Here are seven things we have learned ahead of the new season.

So far this transfer window Ipswich Town have spent in the region of £150m on 12 new players — more than the two other promoted clubs, Coventry and Hull.

The club's two marquee signings have been Julio Enciso for £26m from Strasbourg (along with Abdoul Ouattara) and Emersonn from Toulouse for £24m. But could more be on the way?

"We're not done. Seriously, we're not done," said Ashton.

This season will mark the Blues' first foray into full-scale digital ticketing, meaning fans will have to have their tickets on a digital device and then scan them to enter the stadium.

This has sparked some concern for those who don't own a smartphone or struggle with technology.

Ashton stressed the club was "not trying to provide barriers" and urged people to contact them in advance of matchday.

"Whatever you have in way of concerns around digital ticketing... call us, email us, come and see us," he said.

"We'll make sure someone can spend some time with you.

"We are very aware that change is difficult, but we have to move the football club forward. So I'd ask for fans' patience as people get used to this."

Over the summer "considerable work" has been undertaken at Portman Road.

Changes include safe standing in the Sir Bobby Robson Stand, an extension to fan facilities and improvements to accessibility facilities, which Ashton said were "better than we've ever had".

During the works, there was a surprise when part of the roof of the stadium, from the 1950s, was rediscovered, having been concealed and built over.

"You never quite know at Portman Road what you're going to find, so we had to deal with that, which is all good fun," said Ashton.

In addition to improvements to the club's stadium, Ipswich has a new state-of-the-art training ground, which cost £30m.

It includes a new first team building and better facilities for the Academy and the women's teams, with the players using it for the first time this week.

Ashton said "there is nothing like it in the East of England".

"It's a real elite development centre and everything that you want in a modern training ground is there," he said.

"It's incredible and it's something that we are very, very proud of."

After the shock and sudden departure of former manager Kieran McKenna weeks after securing his third promotion with Town, attention turned to who would replace him.

Former Wolves boss, and Norwich City player, Gary O'Neil was unveiled as the new head coach in June – a decision which garnered a mixed reaction from supporters.

Following four wins from the team's last four pre-season friendlies, any concerns fans may have had may have just started to dissipate.

"What I've seen is someone fit into a club and a culture really quickly; he's had to do it at a breakneck speed and that's never easy," said Ashton.

"But he's been first class - his morals, the way he interacts with people and his work ethic have been superb."

As it happened: Ipswich Town bus parade 2026

For all the jubilation and excitement when Town were promoted back to the top flight for the first time in 22 years in 2024, their return ended with a bit of a whimper and immediate relegation.

The club will, of course, be extremely keen to avoid a repeat of that this time round, but are the Tractor Boys finally ready to compete with the big boys? Ashton thinks so.

"People will say I am overly optimistic, too brave and put pressure on people, but you have to take a bite - you can worry about how you chew it later," he said.

"As long as it doesn't choke you, you're going to be all right. So I think we should try and take a big bite out of the season and be the best versions of ourselves.

"Why can't we do what Sunderland have done and what Brighton have done, and what Bournemouth have done and what Forest have done?

"It's not going to be easy, but I refuse to be defeatist and I want us to push on."

In order for the club to stand a chance of emulating the success of the teams that have defied relegation before them, Ashton believes the 12th man will be incredibly important.

Not least when the team performs at home, which he said could really make all the difference.

"Portman Road will be key – if we win at Portman Road we have a successful season," he said.

"We know what the fortress of Portman Road can do and I think the fans can genuinely make a difference here."

title: Santos FC adds 700,000m² site for new academy training ground
description: Santos FC has taken an important step toward expanding its sports infrastructure by acquiring a plot of land of approximately 700,000 square meters in São Vicente, intended for the development of the...
fullText:
Santos FC has taken an important step toward expanding its sports infrastructure by acquiring a plot of land of approximately 700,000 square meters in São Vicente, intended for the development of the new Youth Academy Training Center. The acquisition was made possible through an agreement signed with Saint-Gobain, a long-standing commercial partner of the Club, in exchange for commercial and advertising properties.

The negotiation was supported by the City Hall of São Vicente to complete the operation, reinforcing joint efforts in favor of the municipality's development.

"First of all, it is essential to highlight the asset-related importance of this transaction with Saint-Gobain for Santos. It is an area of around 700,000 square meters, and its acquisition represents an important step for the project of the new youth academy training center. Certainly, in the future, we will use this area to expand and modernize the Club's sports infrastructure. Undeniably, this is a milestone for the current management and for Santos FC," said president Marcelo Teixeira.

"We have a historic relationship with Santos and see this agreement as another step in that journey. We believe in the transformative role of sport in society and are confident that this partnership will contribute to the club's future projects. For Saint-Gobain, this is another step in strengthening a relationship that has remained solid over the years," commented Gustavo Siqueira, Vice President of HR and Public Affairs for Saint-Gobain in Latin America.

"It is a great joy to see this transaction succeed. First, because São Vicente is undergoing strong development, especially the Continental Area, where 150,000 people live and which will receive the VLT in the coming years, creating a major development corridor. Second, because Santos Futebol Clube is a global brand, the club where King Pelé played, where Prince Neymar plays, and which will now have the opportunity to see its future and its talents develop on the lands of Brazil's First City. The City Hall of São Vicente, anticipating the legal and environmental issues necessary for the use of the area, after talks with CETESB, requested that the EIA-RIMA be commissioned. This request was granted and will allow projects to be developed in the region while respecting the environment and ensuring the proper use of the area by the club," declared the mayor of São Vicente, Kayo Amado.

The next steps related to the development of the new sports complex include carrying out the applicable environmental studies and procedures, including the process before CETESB and obtaining the necessary licenses and authorizations.

To make the construction of the new training center feasible, Santos FC is working on structuring a specific investment fund to finance the implementation of the project. The model is under development and will be presented after the project's technical consolidation.

title: Red Sox reactions: Willson Contreras hits Boston’s longest homer of 2026, overshadowing Rafael Devers’ return
description: Instant reactions from the Red Sox’ 6-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Friday at Fenway Park:
fullText:
BOSTON — Instant reactions from the Red Sox' 6-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Friday at Fenway Park:

1. The Red Sox improved to 69-59 overall and 32-32 at home. The Giants dropped to 52-76 and 23-43 on the road.

2. Willson Contreras recorded both the farthest and hardest hit balls in play by a Red Sox hitter this season when he belted a 452-foot, 116 mph home run over the Green Monster seats in the third inning. The three-run shot put the Red Sox ahead 3-1. He broke his own team highs of 449 feet and 114.9 mph set earlier this season.

It also marked the longest home run hit at Fenway Park this season.

3. It wasn't hit longest ball in play ever. Contreras' longest career home run came in 2021, a 464-foot blast. His hardest hit ball in play came in 2023 with a 117.5 mph exit velocity.

4. Interim manager Chad Tracy interestingly used left-handed rookie Alec Gamboa in the eighth inning with the Red Sox ahead 6-4. Tyron Guerrero's availability was unclear, though Tracy may have been playing the matchups with two left-handed hitters due up. Gamboa got left-handed hitter Bryce Eldridge to line out to left field and left-handed hitter Jung Hoo Lee to ground out to first base. He then struck out Osleivis Basabe swinging to end the inning.

5. Rafael Devers returned to Fenway Park for the first time since Boston traded him to San Francisco on June 15, 2025. And he returned with a bang. He pulled the Giants to within one run at 5-4 in the fourth inning with a 412-foot solo home run to center field.

6. Devers was mostly booed with some light cheering mixed in when he stepped to the plate for the first time in the first inning. After the first inning, the Red Sox played a tribute video. Devers received a round of applause and acknowledged the fans.

7. Devers went 1 for 3 with a home run and walk in his return. Devers, 29, signed with the Red Sox as an amateur international free agent on Aug. 9, 2013, as a 17-year-old. In 1,053 games over nine seasons with Boston, Devers batted .279 with a .859 OPS, 215 home runs, 273 doubles, 12 triples and 696 RBIs.

8. It looked like it could be a pitchers' duel with three-time All-Star Sonny Gray (2.65 ERA in 23 starts) against three-time All-Star Logan Webb (3.50 ERA in 22 starts). But the Red Sox knocked out Webb with two outs in the third inning. The Giants right-hander allowed five runs, six hits and three walks while striking out two.

9. Gray also didn't have his best stuff but earned the win. Friday marked just the fourth time in 24 starts this season that Gray has allowed four or more runs. He allowed four runs, seven hits and two walks while striking out six in six innings. He gave up back-to-back home runs to Drew Gilbert and Devers during a three-run fourth inning for the Giants.

10. The Red Sox went ahead 6-4 with two outs in the sixth inning when Giants right fielder Jung Hoo Lee misread Wilyer Abreu's 107-foot line drive. Lee initially came in and then had to sprint back. The ball went off his glove all the way to the warning track for an RBI triple. Nick Sogard, who had singled with one out, scored.

11. Left-handed reliever Erik Miller — who the Red Sox acquired from the Giants for Marcelo Mayer at the trade deadline — threw a perfect seventh inning and struck out two. He has allowed just one unearned run and has struck out 14 in 8 ⅓ innings with Boston.

12. The Red Sox and Giants will play the second game of their three-game series at 7:15 p.m. Saturday. Left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-2, 4.76 ERA) is scheduled to pitch for the Red Sox while right-hander Blade Tidwell (0-0, 4.33 ERA) will start for San Francisco.

title: Northwestern Has "Best Stadium in Football," Coach David Braun Says
description: Coach David Braun talked up the Wildcats' new stadium while looking ahead to the first game of the season.
fullText:
David Braun is 41 years old and headed into his fourth Division-I football season at the position, all of them with the Northwestern Wildcats.

Braun is one of the younger coaches in the sport and doesn't have as much experience as many of his peers in the Big Ten, but that hasn't stopped him from putting a competitive product on the field in recent years.

The Wildcats are hoping to take things to the next level this season, and the new Ryan Field, seating capacity 35,000, is expected to be a big part of their renaissance as a program.

On Friday, Big Ten Network journalists visited Evanston, Ill. during which they met with Northwestern officials including Braun, who discussed the new stadium and what his team must do to start the season off on a high note.

Expectations for the new Ryan Field are a big part of the positive buzz surrounding the Wildcats this season, and Braun acknowledged it in an interview with Dave Revsine of the Big Ten Network.

"I think there's a balance, there's a lot of excitement around this team, a lot of excitement around what is in store for this season, a new era for offense at Northwestern, and also an attitude of, 'We're not a finished product, there's a lot of work to be done," Braun said.

He pumped the brakes a bit on excitement swirling around the stadium while also talking up to the Big Ten Network audience.

"Also, a clear understanding that as exciting as it is to be moving into the best stadium in all of football on October 2nd, we have one heck of an opponent in South Dakota State coming in here on September 5th, and making sure that as a program, we're narrowing our focus, taking it one day at a time, and putting ourselves in a situation to be at our best for that opening game."

Braun's temperament is understandable considering his team's struggles in recent season openers.

The Wildcats were blitzed 23-3 by the Tulane Green Wave in last season's opening game, but won their 2024 opener by a score of 13-6 against Miami (OH).

Their 2023 opener saw the Wildcats lose 24-7 to the Rutgers Scarlet Knights.

Braun's team should have a decided advantage in the talent and coaching department over the Jackrabbits on Sept. 5 but it still won't be an easy game with nerves on edge and expectations rising in the background.

The Wildcats were 7-6 last season and 8-5 in his first season on campus.

Teams are starting to recognize his program as one on its way up, which could make this season all the more difficult, and exciting, in Evanston, Ill.

title: Packers CB Brandon Cisse says injury vs. Broncos is ‘nothing serious’
description: Cisse went down with a knee injury, after ending up on the wrong side of a double team as a punt gunner vs. Denver
fullText:
Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse got the start opposite Keisean Nixon on the outside against the Denver Broncos on Friday, but he only played one of the first-team defense's two drives in the game after going down with an injury after a punt. According to the Green Bay Press-Gazette's Ryan Wood, Cisse said he got double-teamed as a punter gunner and felt "a little something" in his knee after the play.

Reporters and fans in attendance in Denver saw Cisse go over to the blue tent while the first-team defense played through their second drive, and Cisse later was photographed riding a stationary bike on the sideline.

According to Cisse, the injury is "nothing serious at all," and he wanted to reenter the game, while the club was "being precautionary."

This is your reminder that the Packers have been pretty conservative with injuries this preseason. While players like running back Josh Jacobs, receiver Jayden Reed, tight end Tucker Kraft, left guard Aaron Banks, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, defensive lineman Javon Hargrave, edge defender Dani Dennis-Sutton and cornerback Carrington Valentine all practiced with the team this week, they all were held out of action against the Broncos on Friday.

So you can go ahead and exhale a bit, Packers fans. It seems like Cisse is going to be alright.

There have been no updates on receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, who appeared to exit the game with a possible concussion, or defensive lineman Warren Brinson, who surprisingly didn't get a single snap versus Denver, despite not being listed as a scratch by the team.

title: ‘Put Bo Nix On Ice, He’s Ready’ — PFN Analysts See No Reason to Risk Broncos QB After Comeback From Injury in Preseason Week 2 Stunner
description: Bo Nix gave the Denver Broncos the kind of return they wanted after missing their preseason opener. The quarterback looked comfortable coming back from his ankle injury and showed that being sidelined for months did not affect his play.
fullText:
Bo Nix gave the Denver Broncos the kind of return they wanted after missing their preseason opener. The quarterback looked comfortable coming back from his ankle injury and showed that being sidelined for months did not affect his play.

Nix's performance also offered an early look at Denver's revamped offense, giving PFN analysts another reason to keep their starting quarterback out of harm's way.

Nix needed only two drives to make his presence felt against the Green Bay Packers. He completed six of nine passes for 76 yards and a touchdown, posting a 129.9 passer rating while leading Denver to points on both possessions.

His first series ended with a 21-yard touchdown pass to running back RJ Harvey. The second produced a 53-yard field goal from Wil Lutz before Nix left the game after just 14 snaps.

The quarterback has also established a connection with new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. On the third play of the game, Nix found Waddle for a 35-yard gain, giving Denver an early glimpse of the big-play potential in its revamped passing attack.

That connection becomes even more pronounced alongside Courtland Sutton.

The Broncos are one of only three NFL teams with two wide receivers who posted a top-20 PFN WR Impact Score in 2025. Waddle and Sutton give Nix two high-level options, making an already talented offense even more dangerous in 2026.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

PFN analyst Kyle Soppe immediately highlighted the potential of the new connection. He wrote, "So much to like with this connection. Alpha WR1 season loading. Series ends with Harvey TD catch … only 2 RBs had more a season ago. Defense gets the hype, but this offense will be a PROBLEM."

PFN Director of Media Partnerships Jacob Infante pointed to the overall support around Nix as a reason this season could be important for the quarterback.

Infante wrote, "Bo Nix has all the pieces around him to take another jump in 2026. Great coaching staff, great OL, talented WR duo in Sutton and Waddle. This year is gonna be huge towards determining what his ceiling really is."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

With Nix already looking comfortable in his return, PFN's fantasy football expert Jason Katz sees little value in giving him more preseason work. Katz wrote, "We've seen enough, coach. Put Bo on ice until Week 1. He's ready."

PFN Deputy Editor Alex Kennedy went further in assessing how much Nix's health could mean for Denver's postseason hopes. Kennedy wrote, "If Bo Nix didn't get hurt last postseason, the Broncos would've advanced to the Super Bowl."

NFL Draft analyst Ian Cummings also focused on Nix's movement and accuracy after the injury. Cummings wrote, "In his first action (albeit preseason) back from the ankle injury, I thought Bo Nix looked about as good as you'd want a starting-caliber QB to look. Looked effortless going on the move, timed route breaks perfectly & got this TD with feathery touch."

Nix has already answered the biggest question surrounding his return. After two efficient drives and no obvious limitations, Denver has little reason to expose its starting quarterback to additional preseason hits.

title: Fab Four and Fleming on the phone - England's first-Test takeaways
description: Have England improved or were Pakistan really poor? BBC cricket correspondent Stephan Shemilt analyses the first-Test talking points from Headingley.
fullText:
England's crushing victory over Pakistan was the ideal start to Joe Root's second reign as Test captain.

The home side could not have wished for a more straightforward beginning to a new era as they look to move on from the chaos of the past year.

England's innings win comes with the context of a desperate performance from Pakistan, so any judgements on progress should be reserved for now.

Still, Headingley taught us some things. Here are the takeaways.

England are rebuilding their bowling attack for two reasons.

First, the retirement of Ben Stokes has robbed them not only of inspiration, but of balance.

Secondly, Stokes has followed Stuart Broad, James Anderson, Chris Woakes and, most likely, Mark Wood out of the door. That is 1,871 Test wickets lost in less than three years.

The first stab at a post-Stokes team included four frontline seamers – Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson – supported by the part-time off-breaks of Dan Lawrence.

In helpful conditions, it could not have gone better for England. Robinson and Tongue took eight wickets apiece, while Archer and Atkinson improved after a rusty first innings when they struggled to adapt following a month playing in The Hundred. Lawrence bowled only one over in the match.

Clearly, there will be times when England need a frontline spinner, but there is no consistently Test-class spinner in the country right now.

There is an argument to be made that England should continue to stack their attack with seamers because they are the best bowlers – Root said they "don't know how good they could be".

The likes of Sam Cook and Brydon Carse wait in the wings to step in or provide different skills if necessary, meaning England have a large squad of pacemen to choose from.

A trip to Bangladesh in February will mean England have to find some spin. For now, they should stay in the fast lane.

'Plug him in as attack leader' - England-Pakistan player ratings

It would be 'nice to have choice' over Ashes venues - Root

Jordan Cox has waited a long time for a proper opportunity in Test cricket. Now that it has finally arrived, the Essex batter looks at home at the highest level.

Deputising for the injured Jacob Bethell at number three, Cox impressed with an assured 73. He showed patience and sound judgement, though still had the range of strokes to push the scoring along at a healthy rate without taking risks.

Admittedly, the Pakistan attack Cox faced was far from the most fearsome in Test cricket. None of their seamers had the pace to test his ticker against the short ball.

But, occasionally, players come along and appear instantly suited to Test cricket. Cox seems to fit into that bracket.

His blemish was missing out on the really big score that would have made it impossible for the selectors to leave him out when Bethell returns. Cox potentially has four more innings in this series to make himself undroppable.

If the 25-year-old does demand a place in the XI for the December tour of South Africa and beyond, it leaves England with a dilemma.

Is opener Emilio Gay vulnerable? Bethell is now England's opener in one-day cricket, while Cox opened for Kent at the beginning of his first-class career.

Cox can also keep wicket. Might he put pressure on Jamie Smith? Speaking of whom…

Smith was one of the players who most noticeably wilted under the pressure and scrutiny of the Ashes tour.

He was not helped by a lack of attention to his wicketkeeping in training. Whether it was because a threadbare backroom team was overworked, or England's overall attitude was not good enough, Smith was rarely seen doing the hard yards with the gloves on.

There has been a change this summer. Since joining the coaching staff, former England women's wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor has worked closely with Smith, who has also been able to do more wicketkeeping training with his county Surrey since recovering from a finger injury.

Another circumstance was an injury to Surrey's regular keeper Ben Foakes, one of the best glovemen in the world. It gave Smith three consecutive games behind the stumps in the County Championship in the early part of the season.

The result has been a definite improvement in Smith's keeping for England. It's not as if the 26-year-old ever looked out of place behind the stumps in Test cricket, but he has shown off a greater range of skills this summer, particularly standing up to the fast-medium of Robinson.

At one point, in the third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge, Smith even stood up to the pacey Archer.

Not all progress is linear. Smith's Test batting average has dipped below 40 and he needs to avoid developing a habit for maddening modes of dismissal.

The man who somehow got out to a Marnus Labuschagne bouncer in Sydney tamely holed out for 25 on Friday morning when there was an opportunity for a much bigger contribution.

If Cox or Lawrence fill their batting boots this summer, then England's top-order will become congested. Smith must ensure he does not become vulnerable.

Stephen Fleming, England's new Test coach, is not here. Brendon McCullum's replacement is not due to arrive in the UK until September, by which time the Pakistan series could be over.

Fleming was appointed last month, yet will not take charge of England in a Test until South Africa at Christmas.

The delay has not fully been explained, apart from perhaps a desire to give Fleming a break after almost two decades with Chennai Super Kings.

You will have your own opinions on that one. Being in charge of an Indian Premier League team is intense, but CSK's last match was on 21 May, seven months before England's first Test against the Proteas. Could Fleming, now with one of the biggest jobs in coaching, not have been part of a month-long series against Pakistan?

Either way, Root revealed the New Zealander had been in daily contact during the Headingley Test. "It's been great to have him on the end of the phone," said the captain.

Fleming's influence is not immediately obvious, simply because England were not tested in Leeds.

Should things get more difficult in the remaining two Tests, or if a crucial selection decision needs to be made, perhaps vital input will come from the Flemphone.

'I fear for them' - pundits lament 'desperate times' for Pakistan

A win is a win for England, much needed after only two in their previous 10. However, they should have been better than two wins in 10, and the dismal nature of Pakistan's performance means Root's men can only take limited encouragement from their week in Leeds.

Nothing went right for Pakistan, from the moment captain Babar Azam was ruled out with a thumb injury. Their batting was brittle, their bowling scattergun and their fielding shoddy.

Babar's team beat West Indies in Trinidad earlier this month to earn a 1-1 series draw, yet that was Pakistan's first Test win away from home in more than three years.

They are heavily reliant on winning Tests on spinning pitches, which is why they switched to worn tracks on England's last visit to Pakistan in 2024. When pace bowling becomes the dominant weapon, Pakistan have neither the bowlers nor batters to thrive in the conditions.

Now they head to Lord's, where not one over of spin was bowled in England's shootout win over New Zealand in June.

The surface at the home of cricket could be much different this time around, or a sporty pitch could act as a leveller between the two teams.

Still, the smart money is on another England victory to complete their first series win against anyone in almost two years.

title: A midfielder has reportedly been told that be can also leave Manchester City
description: As of right now, Manchester City are short of midfield options ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season getting under way this weekend. Looking at Enzo Maresca’s squad, there is Elliot Anderson, M...
fullText:
As of right now, Manchester City are short of midfield options ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season getting under way this weekend. Looking at Enzo Maresca's squad, there is Elliot Anderson, Mateo Kovacic, Rico Lewis, Nico O'Reilly, Phil Foden, Nico Gonzalez and Rayan Cherki who will form City's midfield against Bournemouth. Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders left earlier this week, and Bernardo Silva departed when his contract expired at the end of the 2025-26 season. It has now been revealed that Nico Gonzalez has been informed that he can leave Manchester City. If that report is correct, yet another midfield option could leave Enzo Maresca's squad.

Craig Hope of the Daily Mail has reported that Nico Gonzalez has been informed that he can leave Manchester City this summer. Furthermore, it is reported that Newcastle United maintains a strong interest in signing the Spanish midfielder and he is becoming open to the move. Lastly, it is also reported that some of Nico Gonzalez's City teammates are trying to convince him to shun Newcastle's interest and stay at City.

If Craig Hope's report is on the money, Nico Gonzalez is heading for an exit from Manchester City. He'd be another midfielder that City would have to replace. It is seemingly City's plan to replace any player who leaves from this point onwards.

It does seem harsh that Nico Gonzalez has been told he can leave the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. The Spanish midfielder is the only number six in Enzo Maresca's squad. Also, Nico Gonzalez showed during the first half of last season that he can play a role for this City team. He held down the fort superbly well while Rodri was out last season playing in Rodri's role. So there is evidence that Nico is good enough to play in an Enzo Maresca side.

It is hard to see why Pep Guardiola cast Nico Gonzalez aside during the second half of last season. Enzo Maresca seems to prefer Mateo Kovacic in midfield rather than Nico. Maybe Nico isn't thought to be physically strong enough to compete consistently in Manchester City's midfield. Perhaps the issue is that Nico's work in possession isn't up to standard. I'm not sure what the issue but clearly there is something that the majority are missing.

The chances that Nico Gonzalez could leave Manchester City now seem to have increased exponentially. Especially if he has been told he is free to leave the club this summer. You do wonder what the issue with Nico Gonzalez as a player is. He is held in high regard by City fans so it is a puzzling situation.

title: Marion Harding, Mount Vernon play another classic, plus more roundup
description: Marion-area high school football teams opened up the season with Week 1 games. Here's how they fared.
fullText:
In a series that has produced final scores of a touchdown or less in seven of the last nine showdowns, of course Marion Harding and Mount Vernon played it down to the final minutes.

Marcus McGary scored the game-winning touchdown with 2:50 left to lift the Presidents to a 21-17 victory Aug. 21 inside Harding Stadium.

Harding outgained the Yellow Jackets 352 to 144 in yards and 14 to 7 in first downs as the teams combined for five turnovers.

Harding's Mattic Simmers scored the game's first touchdown on a 9-yard run, and Dez Feliciano scored on a 19-yard run. Feliciano was 9 of 16 passing for 117 yards and ran 14 times for 59 yards. McGary led the squad with 97 yards on 14 carries. Theo Collins caught five passes for 48 yards, and Jackson Payne's two catches went for 60 yards. Jaden Jordan intercepted a pass, and Sean Kelly returned a kickoff 60 yards.

Here are more results from around the Marion area during Week 1 of high school football:

Highland's Robby Schmidt only attempted three passes, but he completed two with one going for a touchdown to Hudson Howell as Schmidt finished with 41 yards passing and 110 yards rushing on nine carries, scoring two more TDs.

Nick Hinkle added 85 yards on 16 carries and a touchdown, plus made 12 tackles. Kane Stover produced 17 tackles and forced a fumble, while Zach Riley had nine tackles, and Dylan Wiggand had eight tackles. The Scots combined for six tackles for loss, and Hayden Moore returned a fumble 56 yards.

North Union-Pleasant Week 1: Rivals meet again with Pleasant going to North Union during Week 1

Results from other fall sports: Pleasant second at MOAC golf tourney, plus more Marion-area roundup

Elgin made the road trip to Arlington and took it to the home team as Abram Norton ran for 54 yards on 14 carries with a touchdown and added 11-for-15 passing for 142 yards and two more scores.

Archer Johnston ran for 49 yards and caught four passes for 47 more, adding a TD, while Braydon Lowry ran only five times but finished with 108 yards with an 86-yard touchdown. Finn Van Gundy caught a 32-yard touchdown, and Luke Nelson caught two passes for 40 yards. Cayden Hunt kicked a 26-yard field goal, too.

For the Elgin defense, Drew Brown led everyone with 11 tackles and three tackles for loss, while Zack Bowers and Nelson picked off passes, and Russell Norton recovered two fumbles. T.J. Britton made seven tackles, and Johnston also recovered a fumble.

After a scoreless first quarter, River Valley tied it at 7-7 on an Owen Collins to Carter Myers pass, then took a 9-7 lead after a safety on a kickoff return by Bloom-Carroll. A pair of TD runs by Kyson Cline proved to be the difference as he ended with 236 yards on 25 runs for the Bulldogs. Myers made six catches for 114 yards as Collins was 21-for-42 passing and 219 yards.

Ridgedale dropped one on the road. Lincoln Kramer was 10 of 25 passing for 131 yards, while Billy Wren made six catches for 89 yards, and Kingston McGary caught four for 47 yards for the Rockets. Braxton Roberts led with 64 rushing yards on 16 carries.

On defense for Ridgedale, Wren recorded nine tackles; Roberts ended with five tackles and two sacks; Britton Pottkotter finished with six tackles; and Hunter Hutchinson blocked an extra point attempt.

Martins Ferry made the long road trip from the Ohio River but still jumped out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter before rolling to a 35-6 edge by halftime.

Scoring for MG were Tyler Harr on a 20-yard run, Kolton White on a 35-yard fumble return and Boe Sayers on a 4-yard run. Harr caught both of his team's receptions and rushed 12 times for 86 yards. Sayers ran for 80 yards on 14 tries.

Jackson Welch caught 11 passes for 182 yards, including touchdown strikes of 24 and 56 yards for the Golden Knights. Tanner Miley was 14-for-31 with 228 yards, adding 41 rushing yards on 24 attempts. Brody Beck ran it 13 times for 41 yards, adding an 11-yard TD run.

title: High school football: Desert Hills survives the heat, takes down Timpanogos to improve to 2-0
description: Hosting the Timpanogos Timberwolves Friday night, not even the triple-digit heat or the excessive number of penalties could keep the Desert Hills Thunder from earning a 29-13 victory.  It looked early on that it would be the Wolves striking first, as they marched down to the Desert Hills 20-yard line before ultimately turning the ball over on downs.  It didn’t take long for the Timpanogos defense to make an impact, however, as Jace Spencer hauled in an interception to give the ball back to the offense.
fullText:
Hosting the Timpanogos Timberwolves Friday night, not even the triple-digit heat or the excessive number of penalties could keep the Desert Hills Thunder from earning a 29-13 victory.

It looked early on that it would be the Wolves striking first, as they marched down to the Desert Hills 20-yard line before ultimately turning the ball over on downs.

It didn't take long for the Timpanogos defense to make an impact, however, as Jace Spencer hauled in an interception to give the ball back to the offense.

Just one play later, quarterback Logan Holloway found Spencer to make it 7-0 with just over six minutes to play in the first quarter.

After the Wolves missed a field goal a few possessions later, the Thunder moved their way down the field late in the first quarter thanks to some strong runs by Seth Brown.

The first quarter clock expired, but Brown wasn't done. Quarterback Deacon Virgin delivered a pass to the junior running back, who took it 46 yards to the house to open the second period.

The ensuing two-point try was successful, putting Desert Hills in front 8-7.

Just moments later, a Wolves turnover led to another Thunder score as Virgin once again made a deep connection, tossing a 30-yard score to Tagg Brinton to make it 15-7 just over two minutes into the second quarter.

It seemed as though Desert Hills might turn the game into a rout from there, but a missed field goal and a turnover on downs inside its own 10-yard line made sure the score stayed 15-7 heading to the halftime break.

The Thunder added another score on the first drive of the second half, as an 8-yard run by Brown pushed the advantage to 22-7.

Both teams traded punches for the rest of the third quarter before Timpanogos finally found the end zone again early in the fourth.

Holloway connected with Zack McCann from eight yards out, but the two-point attempt failed, making it a 22-13 score.

The Wolves would once again force a turnover on the next Desert Hills possession but were unable to come away with points.

An Isaac Hall 31-yard run with two minutes to go would be the final tally, as the Thunder claimed the 29-13 victory to improve to 2-0.

One of the keys to victory for Desert Hills was slowing down the explosive Holloway, who racked up five touchdowns in Week 1 vs. Juan Diego.

Against the Thunder, he had just two.

"We executed it perfectly," senior defensive tackle Asher Snow said of the game plan to stop Holloway. "Our coaches have harped on us to finish and just be out there and be physical, and I love to see the team like that."

On the offensive side, Brown led the way, notching both a receiving and rushing score.

"(The Wolves) were very physical up front, so I was just trying my best," Brown said of his big night.

As the Thunder sit at 2-0, they have already surpassed early expectations. A year ago, they won just two games all season.

"That's the plan," Desert Hills first-year head coach Tanner Balderree said of surprising people. "Everything we've done is to be what we feel like we can be and what we should be.

"I feel like we're getting to where we should be with the kids and coaches that we have, and we're starting to see that potential come out."

title: Week 1 Roundup: "The Champ Monds Show" dazzles, Vero Beach blanks Jensen Beach
description: Notre Dame commit Champ Monds accounted for five touchdowns to lead Vero Beach past Jensen Beach 34-0. Four other teams had shutouts Friday.
fullText:
VERO BEACH — Fans in the stands had to wait a while to catch this regular season's first episode of "The Champ Monds Show."

But as has been the case through the prior two seasons, the Vero Beach quarterback made it a must-see experience.

The four-star Notre Dame commit accounted for five total touchdowns while his defense played a supporting role during the Vero's 34-0 season-opening shutout over Jensen Beach on Friday, Aug. 21, 2026 from the Billy Living Field at the Citrus Bowl.

On Senior Night, the senior quarterback posted three touchdown passes to three different receivers while rushing in two more scores.

"Obviously, our quarterback had another great night," Vero Beach head coach Lenny Jankowski said.

Sign up and save to watch the NFHS Network

The game started 75 minutes after its scheduled 7 p.m. kickoff due to a lengthy lightning delay. It was later called with 10 minutes, 45 seconds remaining in regulation after lightning reappeared around 10:30 p.m.

The home side did not produce a first down through its first three possessions. However, the third series did result in the game's first points. Facing a second-and-10, Monds hit Marcus Melbourne in stride on a slant pattern, with the senior wide receiver splitting through the Falcons secondary for a 72-yard touchdown reception.

Monds spread the love as the night wore on before pulling down the ball when opportunity presented itself.

He connected with junior Micah Roberts and senior Marc Jones for 14-yard scoring passes on the following two possessions. The quarterback then capped an eight-play 88-yard drive with a 2-yard rush, putting Vero Beach up 27-0 with four seconds left before halftime. After Vero's defense forced a turnover on downs to open the third quarter, Monds ended his night with a 13-yard scamper into the end zone.

"Monds was coming in cool. I've known his family for a long time, so we knew what to expect from him," Jensen Beach head coach Tim Caffey said.

Monds finished the night 12-for-14 passing for 195 yards and added four carries for 25 yards. He completed passes to six different receivers, which according to Jankowski is partially by design and partially a product of the quarterback's decision making.

"Really and truly we have five eligible receivers on each and every play, and Champ has a good understanding of what we're trying to do on offense and where defenses are vulnerable," Jankowski said. "Nobody wants to run a play through the teeth of the defense. So we're trying to capitalize where they may be vulnerable and he's the right guy to do it."

Johns was Monds' favorite target. The St. Lucie West Centennial transfer had four receptions for 77 yards.

What a difference a week can make.

After allowing 54 points in a Kickoff Classic defeat to John Carroll Catholic, the Eagles nearly matched that total when they throttled the Trojans on the road.

"We watched the film and saw all the mistakes that we made. We just tried to clean it up and correct that," Centennial head coach Alfred Yates said. "It was just getting back to the basics and getting them sharp on the plays that we've been going through all week."

According to Yates, the visitors controlled the line of scrimmage. On offense, linemen were aggressive to their blocks while the team's collection of running backs gashed through the Lake Worth front. The Eagles rallied to the ball on defense after struggling to complete tackles against the Rams last week.

Aalijah Thomas scored twice on the ground while Malik Jefferson, Marquez Lighthouse and Keslor Fanescar each added a rushing touchdown. Elsewhere, Daiquiri Boswell tossed two scores and Reilly Viau had a punt return touchdown.

Centennial led 27-6 at the half and added 13 points in each of the third and fourth quarters to secure Yates' first win as head coach.

"It feels good getting it out of the way so we can just focus on the next game," he said. "I'll sit back and reflect on it later, but I'm already looking forward to game planning for the next game."

title: Cavaliers GM Koby Altman pens a heartfelt farewell for Max Strus after the latest trade
description: Max Strus may have played for the Cavaliers for only three seasons, but he left an indelible mark.
fullText:
Cavaliers GM Koby Altman pens a heartfelt farewell for Max Strus after the latest trade originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Max Strus signed a four-year contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2023 in a sign-and-trade with the Miami Heat. At the time, it was a fantastic decision for the Cavaliers because they lacked perimeter shooting beyond their backcourt of Darius Garland and Donovan Mitchell.

During the three seasons he played for the Cavaliers, Strus was a positive for the team. He provided good perimeter shooting, and he had the intangibles that helped the Cavaliers succeed. Unfortunately, his time with the team ended in the 2026 offseason, which involved another sign-and-trade.

Strus is now a member of the Los Angeles Clippers roster, where he is reunited with Garland. It is a promising landing spot, especially since they have decided to fully commit to a new direction by dealing Kawhi Leonard away to the Toronto Raptors.

While they still have no resolution with that controversial player, they are making good decisions beyond him. Signing Rui Hachimura, getting Strus, and drafting Keaton Wagler were all good decisions, which makes it a great landing spot for Strus.

MORE: The trade grades for every party involved in Peyton Watson's move to the Cavaliers

Now that he has left the Cavaliers, it seems he was a favorite within the Cavs organization. Not only did the players like Mitchell show him love, but it seems the GM, Koby Altman, loved having Strus around. That is why he penned a heartfelt goodbye to the sharpshooter.

"We want to recognize and thank Max for everything he has meant to the Cavaliers. Over the past several seasons, Max became an important part of our team, our culture, and our identity... He was an important part of our continued rise and the sustainable success we have worked to build, and we are incredibly grateful for the way he represented the Cavaliers every day," Altman said about Strus after making the trade for Watson.

Altman had the right idea of trading for Peyton Watson, who solves a lot of problems the Cavs had with their small forward woes. Thankfully, he is an athletic wing who will also defend and be a reliable offensive player, something they have needed for a long time ever since they had Isaac Okoro for a long time.

title: Drought leaves sports clubs 'praying for rain'
description: Some grass pitches are dry and hard and clubs are struggling to water their playing surfaces.
fullText:
Periods of drought and prolonged hot, dry weather has had a major effect on sports clubs across south-west England, who are feeling the strain.

The unprecedented weather has left some grass pitches extremely dry and hard for clubs with little to no irrigation, with many dependent on meaningful rainfall for recovery.

A hosepipe ban was put in force on 9 August across Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly as the conditions put "significant pressure" on the regions water supplies.

South West Water said sports pitches and surfaces were "exempt from hosepipe bans where watering is necessary", so long as it took place outside peak hours of 08:00-10:00 BST and 17:00-21:00 BST.

Bill Martin, chairman and assistant groundsman at Plymouth Cricket Club, said he had "never seen the pitch so dry".

He said this summer has been particularly difficult as a groundsman because "it had been a summer of two halves".

He said the first six weeks it was "very very wet" but since then it had been two months without significant rain.

"We've got one tap and one hose, so the real challenge has been getting water on to the surface, particularly the playing wickets.

He said without water, the ground became very dry and the grass disappeared and turned to dust, which was both difficult to play and dangerous.

"Cricket is a fine weather sport, so we've not had interruptions, we've not lost any games and we've been able to play a lot of cricket in the sunshine which has been great, but in terms of actually looking after the ground and preparing decent pitches to play on, it makes it very hard work."

"Unusually for cricketers we have been praying for rain."

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) announced the start of the community rugby season had been delayed until 21 September because of concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions. While the Football Association issued guidance which said there was "no blanket suspension of football on dry grass pitches" but the priority was to keep "football playing safely".

Lynton Football Club made the decision to postpone their opening fixture of the season.

In a post on social media the club said three players had suffered "serious injuries", with two "undoubtedly" because of the hard surfaces and would not risk any further injuries on a "rock hard almost concrete like pitch".

Nick Rich from Saltash Rugby Football Club said he had "never seen the pitch as parched as it is at the moment".

"It's rock solid out there. If you turned the tables and it was frozen in winter, you would not play a game of rugby on it."

He said the decision to delay the season was a good thing for both rugby and safety but did mean there was a delay in revenue for the club.

Just 15 months ago the club reseeded the pitch at great cost.

He said further reseeding took place earlier this summer and they had "waited for rain so the grass seed would germinate and we haven't had it yet".

"There's been some watering going on but clearly nowhere enough and we've put thousands of gallons on it."

It is a similar story at Ivybridge Bowls Club who have "struggled to keep up" with the amount of watering required during the high temperatures.

Malcolm Johnson, club captain and groundsman, said the club's watering system was small and the green should be watered at least four times a day to keep it growing, but was unable to do that because of the hosepipe restrictions imposed.

"We've got to a point now where we have to leave it as it is and are going to have to start from scratch again in the spring."

A small amount of rain caused a game to be called off on Wednesday because the water was not draining away quickly enough.

Johnson said "the surface is that hard that it is not being absorbed - we would like to spike it, we've got all the machinery to do that but it's just too hard".

title: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy Admits Plan With RB Kaleb Johnson
description: As questions continue to surround the Pittsburgh Steelers‘ running back position behind Jaylen Warren, head coach Mike McCarthy decided to grant Kaleb Johnson a big opportunity on Friday night.After only receiving two carries in Pittsburgh’s preseason opener on August 13, Johnson touched the ball 12 times in the 17-0 loss to the Jets. And while, […] The post Steelers HC Mike McCarthy Admits Plan With RB Kaleb Johnson appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
As questions continue to surround the Pittsburgh Steelers' running back position behind Jaylen Warren, head coach Mike McCarthy decided to grant Kaleb Johnson a big opportunity on Friday night.

After only receiving two carries in Pittsburgh's preseason opener on August 13, Johnson touched the ball 12 times in the 17-0 loss to the Jets. And while, unlike the Steelers 28-9 win over the Packers, the offense struggled to move the ball consistently and failed to put any points on the scoreboard with New York in town, Johnson attempted to make the most out of his chance to impress.

Johnson ran for 39 yards on 10 rushing attempts, averaging 3.9 yards per carry. He also caught two passed for 15 yards.

McCarthy even admitted that "it was a conscious effort to give him (Johnson) more opportunities" when asked by reporters about the workload for the 23-year-old back after the game.

Mike McCarthy on Kaleb Johnson playing so much:"It was a conscious effort to give him more opportunities."

Johnson had a game-high 10 carries and gained 39 yards.

— Chris Adamski (@C_AdamskiTrib) August 22, 2026

Johnson did appear in 10 games as a rookie in 2025, but was only handed 28 carries. He totaled 68 yards on the ground and one reception for nine yards off two targets overall throughout the season.

So while Johnson, Pittsburgh's 2025 third round pick out of the University of Iowa, still remains an unknown and has yet to really prove himself in the NFL, it's notable that his new head coach – he played for Mike Tomlin in his first year – remains interested in seeing what he can do if given more of a shot. And it's now likely that Johnson earned another long look in the Steelers' preseason finale on Thursday, August 27th in Buffalo.

Depth chart wise, Johnson is still behind veteran newcomer Rico Dowdle, coming off a season in which he surpassed 1,000 yards with 1,076 and scored six touchdowns in 2025 with Carolina, and Warren, who averaged 4.5 yards per carry and racked up 958 yards as Pittsburgh's featured back last season.

It will now remain to be seen how Johnson is handled and what his future on the Steelers' roster under McCarthy looks like.

title: Edman’s extra-inning heroics give Dodgers walk-off win
description: Max Muncy hit another go-ahead home run in the first inning
fullText:
Tommy Edman helped power the Dodgers (78-51) to a 5-4 walk-off victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates (63-67) Friday night at Dodger Stadium.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched another gem, striking out nine over 6 2/3 innings. Kyle Hurt blew the lead in relief, but Edgardo Henriquez and Even Phillips preserved the tie long enough for the offense to come back for the extra-innings win and fourth straight win for the Boys in Blue.

The Pirates captured a 1-0 lead very quickly in the first against Yamamoto. Brandon Lowe singled just past Freddie Freeman at first base, and then Bryan Reynalds was hit by a Yamamoto cutter. Nick Gonzales jumped on a first-pitch splitter for a RBI single to center.

Max Muncy continues to clobber baseballs at Dodger Stadium. After all, he is the Dodger Stadium home run king. He took a Chandler high fastball for a ride, and the go-ahead home run gave the Dodgers a 2-1 lead in the bottom of the first.

Ahoy, Max! pic.twitter.com/hZiWEWpLAJ

Yamamoto struck out the side in the second utilizing his repertoire of pitches masterfully including his four-seam fastball, splitter, and sinker.

Yoshinobu strikes out the side. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/GF4w0i5aHq

The Dodger fans roared in support for Kyle Tucker when he stepped into the batter's box in the bottom of the second. The struggling outfielder went 0-for-4 with a walk on the night.

The Pirates tied it up in the third with two outs thanks to the same culprits who scored in the first. Lowe hit a ground-rule-double, and Gonzales brought him home with another RBI single.

The Dodgers opened the bottom of the third with back-to-back hits against Chandler from Hunter Feduccia and Shohei Ohtani. With runners at the corners, the Dodgers didn't test the arm of Oneil Cruz on a Freeman liner.

Andy Pages got hit with a 100-mph pitch on his left hand to load the bases. He stayed in the game at first, but Kiké Hernández replaced Pages in center field in the fifth inning due to a left hand contusion.

X-rays showed a fracture in Pages' hand, Dave Roberts said. It's not expected to be a season-ending injury, but he's expected to be out for at least four weeks. https://t.co/F8QnainysK

Mookie Betts gave the Dodgers back the lead with a two-out two-RBI single to center.

Mookie knocks in a pair! pic.twitter.com/8hk3bu8ruA

The Pirates got their first base hit against Yamamoto since the third inning when Jake Mangum led off with a double in the seventh.

In the top of the 8th inning, the relief corps faltered once again, allowing the Pirates to strike back and tie the game at 4–4, officially wiping away Yamamoto's chance at a well-deserved win.

The Pirates didn't go down easy and continued to apply pressure to the Dodgers bullpen. Reynalds opened the eighth with a double against Hurt. Cruz evened the game with one swing of the bat. He crushed a four-seamer right down the middle for a two-run shot.

Mason Montgomery retired the Dodgers in order in the ninth including two strikeouts to send the game into extra innings.

Reynalds led off the 10th for Pittsburgh with a single against Phillips. Gonzales struck out after a battle of an at-bat. Cruz is intentionally walked to load the bases with one out for Henry Davis. Dave Roberts looked like a genius after David grounded into a double play to preserve the 4-4 tie.

Alex Call got the call to pinch-hit for Muncy and bunt over the ghost runner in the bottom of the 10th. This time Roberts' strategy failed. Call struck out and failed to move the runner over. It was easily Call's worst at-bat of the season.

Betts was intentionally walked by Gregory Soto, but Tucker chopped a force out thereafter.

Edman got the job done. He came up huge with a clutch walk-off hit to left field on a two-strike count to give the Dodgers the win.

Tommy Edman's 10th-inning base knock wins it for the @Dodgers 🔥 pic.twitter.com/moaw6nU8VA

Home runs: Max Muncy (26); Oneil Cruz (16)

WP — Evan Phillips (1-2): 1 IP, 1 hits, no runs, 1 walk, 1 strikeouts (18 pitches)

LP — Gregory Soto (5-4): 2/3 IP, 1 hit, 1 run, 1 walk, 1 strikeout (14 pitches)

The Dodgers and Pirates continue the series on Saturday (4:15 p.m. PT, FOX). Tarik Skubal (7-7, 2.85 ERA, 0.96 WHIP) takes the ball for the Dodgers. Jared Jones (2-5, 4.78 ERA, 1.20 WHIP) starts for the Bucs.

title: Details of Liverpool’s rejected proposals to sign Real Madrid starlet
description: Endrick is back in Madrid for the new season and already working hard to impress Jose Mourinho in his early days at the club.A fitness setback has forced him to miss out on Real Madrid’s season open...
fullText:
Endrick is back in Madrid for the new season and already working hard to impress Jose Mourinho in his early days at the club.

A fitness setback has forced him to miss out on Real Madrid's season opener later today, but it is clear that Jose Mourinho counts on the player after the management and administration jointly decided that the player must stay.

Liverpool, however, made a notable attempt to lure the player away from the Spanish giants earlier this week. As reported, their effort was futile and Fabrizio Romano now reveals more details on what the Merseyside club had in mind.

Indeed, as reported by the Italian journalist, Liverpool did indeed make direct contact with Real Madrid for the young Brazilian's transfer and they did not have any hard and fast demands.

Endrick is in Mourinho's plans. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

They wanted to see if there was any possibility at all for Los Blancos to open up to transferring the player, primarily as a loan with an option to purchase at the end of the season.

Concurrently, they were also willing to go for a direct permanent transfer with a massive proposal and fee.

For Real Madrid and Endrick, however, neither option was seen as feasible and Florentino Perez and Jose Mourinho both slammed the door shut.

As matters stand, there is nothing that can make Endrick leave Real Madrid this summer for the player has made up his mind on staying and making it big at the club of his dreams.

Carlos Espi's arrival is a direct threat to Endrick's place. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

What the youngster is not happy about, however, is the club signing Carlos Espi after Gonzalo Garcia, for he saw it as a sign that Real Madrid do not trust him.

Word has it that the player is currently determined to stay and fight for a spot, but that hr will review his situation in January.

If his minutes are not where he expects, there is every chance he may push for a loan departure midway through the season.

Everything will come down to where Mourinho places the striker on his pecking order and the importance the player enjoys, at least as an option off the bench.

title: Should Commanders pursue Steelers star if he were available?
description: If the Steelers chose to listen to offers for CB Joey Porter Jr., the Commanders would make sense. Just don't count on it.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders had the rare opportunity to add a difference-making player in training camp earlier this month when they signed wide receiver Stefon Diggs. Top players are generally not available this late in the year unless there are questions. Whether it's injuries, age, or off-field issues, there are reasons why good players can still be signed in August.

Diggs appears to be a big hit for the Commanders. But what if Washington could add another potential difference-maker? This one would cost significantly more, but it would be a player at your weakest defensive position. That player is Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

Remember the 2023 NFL Draft, when Porter was often projected to Washington in various mock drafts? Instead, Ron Rivera shocked everyone by passing over Christian Gonzalez and Porter to select Emmanuel Forbes with the No. 16 overall pick. Gonzalez has gone on to become one of the NFL's best cornerbacks in three seasons, while Porter is off to a phenomenal start in his career.

So why has Porter's name recently been floated in trade rumors? Pittsburgh hasn't, but NFL insider Jordan Schultz says other teams have "wondered" whether the Steelers would part with Porter if the two sides can't agree to a new long-term deal. Porter is now eligible for an extension and presumably wants to be paid like one of the NFL's top cornerbacks.

#Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a name multiple teams around the NFL have wondered about as a potential trade target, per sources.

JPJ is in the final year of his rookie contract, and with where the CB market is, teams have wondered if Pittsburgh could ultimately be open to a… pic.twitter.com/0t1CX9laOQ

If the Steelers made Porter available, he is the type of player Washington could and, perhaps should, pursue. Currently, Washington's top three cornerbacks are Trey Amos, Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson, with three players 30 and older battling for what is likely the final two cornerback spots. Amos has barely practiced all summer, although he's expected back soon. Sainristil was phenomenal as a rookie, but struggled badly last season.

The Commanders believe an improved pass rush will help their cornerbacks. They are correct. And while the position may not be as much of a concern now as it was a month ago, questions remain.

Even if the Steelers were to listen to offers for Porter, Washington GM Adam Peters is unlikely to pay a premium trade price, either multiple picks or a first-round pick, and then have to pay top-five position money for Porter.

On Friday, one Steelers insider said Pittsburgh hasn't received any calls on Porter and has no intention of trading him, barring "an insane offer."

Everybody has a price. And it only takes one team to pay that price. Don't expect it to be Washington.

This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Should Commanders pursue Steelers star if he were available?

title: Super agent offers €40 million-rated Barcelona homegrown star to AC Milan – Romano
description: Alejandro Balde’s future at Barcelona is beginning to attract increasing attention, with the young defender no longer viewed as completely untouchable at the Catalan club.The latest Barcelona transf...
fullText:
Alejandro Balde's future at Barcelona is beginning to attract increasing attention, with the young defender no longer viewed as completely untouchable at the Catalan club.

The latest Barcelona transfer news has brought AC Milan into the picture, although the Italian club is yet to take a step towards signing the 22-year-old.

According to Fabrizio Romano, Balde's agent Jorge Mendes has offered the Barcelona defender to AC Milan as he explores the market for his client.

However, the Italian giants are not currently planning a move of that size, particularly with Barcelona believed to value the La Masia graduate at more than €40 million.

Right now, Balde is said to be happy in Barcelona and is not looking for an exit.

His priority is to stay and fight for his place, even though his position in Hansi Flick's plans is no longer as secure as it once appeared.

Not long ago, Balde looked set to be Barcelona's undisputed long-term answer at left-back.

Alejandro Balde has been offered to AC Milan. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

A product of La Masia, the Spanish defender made a major impression after breaking into the first team and quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young full-backs in European football.

However, the situation has changed.

The permanent arrival of Joao Cancelo has increased competition and complicated the picture for Balde.

His route to regular first-team football is no longer as clear, while Hansi Flick is also understood to have some doubts about the defender.

That does not mean Barcelona are pushing Balde out of the club. However, the possibility of an Alejandro Balde transfer is no longer completely off the table.

Jorge Mendes recently met with Barcelona directors to discuss the futures of several of his clients, with Balde among the players whose situations were assessed.

Barcelona have been aware for some time that a summer departure could become a realistic possibility under the right circumstances.

Barcelona are open to selling Alejandro Balde. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

According to Romano, Mendes has already tested the possibility of a move to AC Milan by offering Balde's services to the Serie A side.

At present, though, Milan are not planning to commit to a transfer worth more than €40 million.

Barcelona's asking price is proving to be a major obstacle for potential clubs, particularly given the financial scale of such a deal.

Meanwhile, Manchester United have also entered the conversation.

The Premier League club contacted Mendes this week to ask about the conditions required to sign Balde. However, there has been no official offer from Manchester United, and the situation remains at an early stage.

The Barcelona defender himself is not believed to be driving a move.

Balde wants to remain at Camp Nou and compete for his position, meaning any transfer would depend heavily on Barcelona's stance and whether an interested club is willing to meet their valuation.

title: With miracle cure to the final?! Reserves equal DFB-Pokal record
description: "Berlin, Berlin, we're staying in Berlin," echoed through the streets of the German capital in 1993. The Old Lady had finally made it to the DFB Cup final in its own stadium. Well, almost. How almost?...
fullText:
"Berlin, Berlin, we're staying in Berlin," echoed through the streets of the German capital in 1993. The Old Lady had finally made it to the DFB Cup final in its own stadium. Well, almost. How almost?

The first team had already been knocked out in the round of 16 by Bayer 04 Leverkusen (0:1). Okay, so how could Hertha still have been in the final? Simple enough: the second team — affectionately known as the Hertha Bubis — went on one of the most incredible runs in German cup history, one that remains unmatched to this day.

The third-division side certainly wasn't thinking about a final yet when, after a bye, it faced SGK Heidelberg in the second round of the cup. But the amateur squad, made up of students, trainees, and schoolkids, beat the then-Oberliga side 3:0. The Bubis also cleared the next hurdle against VfB Leipzig (4:2) with flying colors. But after the draw for the round of 16, no one believed in another cup upset.

On November 6, 1992, the team led by young Carsten Ramelow — who would later become a Germany international — faced none other than defending champions Hannover 96. What can we say. Hertha's reserves sensationally won 4:3 and promptly rewrote the final song "We're going to Berlin" into "Berlin, Berlin, we're staying in Berlin!" Was their subsequent quarterfinal opponent Nürnberg thrilled about that? Hertha knocked out the Club too with a 2:1 win. "The worst part is that Hertha deserved to go through," admitted Nürnberg star and Germany international Dieter Eckstein after the cup exit. Maybe it was simply down to some kind of "miracle cure" the team had? A ritual that made cup dreams come true?

Before every match, the team would go eat at Pizzeria San Remo in Berlin-Wedding and, according to coach Jochem Ziegert, were allowed to enjoy "spaghetti until they drop." Loaded with carbohydrates, the third-division side then swept aside Chemnitz in the semifinal — coached by legendary manager Hans Meyer.

"You are no superhumans, no heroes, as the media currently like to report. You are Herthaner who love football, from number one to number seven. From number eight all the way to number 25, known from Lake Constance and even in Gdańsk," Hertha press spokesman Klaus-Dieter Vollrath then recited in a poem dedicated to the Hertha Bubis.

Whether it was the pasta, the love of football, or simply a lot of luck — it didn't matter. Hertha BSC's reserve team had pulled off a football miracle and reached the cup final against Bayer 04 Leverkusen. Hardly anyone talks about the final itself nowadays.

Once again, the Hertha Bubis delivered a strong performance, but in the end they had to accept a 0:1 defeat against Bayer's star-studded squad. Ulf Kirsten scored the winner for Leverkusen, but the loudest cheers in the Olympiastadion were for Hertha's reserves. The amateurs had made history.

Never before had a reserve team reached the DFB Cup final. And that will very likely remain the case forever. Since 2008, clubs have only been allowed to enter the competition with one team.

At least Arminia Bielefeld showed in 2025 that third-division teams can still make it to the final. So miracles do still happen. Just not one like the Hertha Bubis'.

fullText:
Is Agentic scores the public parts of a website that AI agents can discover, retrieve, understand, and use. Essential checks carry most of the score and cover fundamentals such as server-rendered content, correct HTTP behavior, clear document structure, recoverable errors, and usable controls.

Recommended checks activate when scan evidence indicates that a site offers an API, OAuth flow, GraphQL endpoint, MCP server, developer portal, or commerce surface. Checks that do not apply are excluded rather than counted as failures, so a public website is not penalized for omitting an interface it does not provide.

Start with failed Essential checks because they describe the baseline an ordinary agent needs. Then review Recommended gaps that match the product’s real capabilities. Every finding includes the evidence observed during the scan and, where available, a concrete recommendation that can be copied into an implementation workflow.

Emerging formats can earn limited bonus credit, but their absence never lowers a score. After shipping a fix, rescan the same public URL to replace the latest report with a fresh snapshot while retaining a stable URL for sharing and comparison.

Each report also includes an observed agent journey showing how one agent navigated the site and where it encountered friction. That run is supporting evidence rather than part of the numeric score, because one task cannot represent every agent, user goal, or production condition.

Developers and agents can retrieve completed reports through the public JSON API or the Is Agentic MCP server. The docs describe the endpoints, schemas, authentication policy, and machine-readable OpenAPI description without changing the browser scoring experience.

Public report URLs are stable and render their latest completed score in the initial HTML response, so crawlers do not need to execute JavaScript or wait for a client-side fetch. An agent that asks for text/markdown receives a compact Markdown representation at the same canonical URL, while software integrations can request structured JSON from the report API. Shared caches keep the HTML and Markdown representations separate through the HTTP Vary header.

The MCP server exposes the same completed report as a read-only tool with a declared input schema, structured output, and an optional interactive score card for hosts that support MCP Apps. None of these machine interfaces starts a scan, mutates the target site, or requires a credential. If a completed report does not exist yet, the browser report URL is the place to start and observe a new scan.

A report describes evidence available from one public URL at a particular time. Status codes, crawler policies, rendered content, documentation, advertised APIs, and emerging agent protocols can all change after the snapshot. Is Agentic stores the newest completed result for quick retrieval and may refresh stale reports in the background while keeping the previous completed score visible until replacement evidence is ready.

Use the report as a prioritized technical review, not as a guarantee that every model or browser automation system will complete every task. Private pages, authenticated workflows, geographic differences, bot defenses, temporary outages, and user-specific state can produce behavior that a public scan cannot observe. Security, accessibility, privacy, legal compliance, and business quality each require their own dedicated review.

title: Apple Guts Vision Pro Gaming and Immersive Video Teams, Trims Siri Staff

title: The Instant team joins OpenAI
description: The Instant team is joining OpenAI. Instant Cloud runs until August 31st, 2027.
fullText:
The Instant team joins OpenAIInstant2 min readWe have a big announcement to make today: the Instant team is joining OpenAI.
We started Instant to make it easy for you to build delightful apps. Over the last few years we saw that most of our users began to use Instant through agents. Agents already empower many of us to build more ambitious things, and we’re only at the beginning stages of what they can do. We are excited to join OpenAI and bring intelligence to as many people as we can.
If you are a user of Instant Cloud, this is what the news means for you:

New signups are closed. Existing users should migrate off of Instant Cloud within the next 12 months. Any subscriptions that were started after July 31st, 2026 will be fully refunded.
On August 31st, 2027, all cloud apps will shut down. Backups will stay available for 12 more months, until August 31st, 2028.
We’ve written a guide to help you self-host Instant and migrate your apps too. All of Instant is open source, and we’ve worked to make the migration process as seamless as possible.

The idea behind Instant started in 2021. We shared a blog post about a database in the browser. It was only an idea, but the more apps we built, the more we saw the need for it. We joined YC in 2022, built a prototype, and shared a version zero.
Turning a prototype into something production-grade was a long journey. The work was hard, but there were many moments of joy. [1] Very early on Daniel joined the team and helped solve some of the gnarliest problems in sync tech. Our community grew, more folks joined [2], and we officially open sourced. From there it was a maelstrom of feedback and making Instant better. When time came to really make our TypeScript SDKs ergonomic, Drew joined the team and did just that. From there, over 17,000 users got to try Instant. They made 400,000 apps, and those apps processed about 2.5 billion transactions.
If you are an Instant customer, it’s been an honor building for you.

(Right to left) Joe Averbukh, Stepan Parunashvili, Daniel Woelfel, Drew Harris
Footnotes

One time we shared a post on X, where colors synced in React Native. We were so excited at the milestone, that we think our smile might have gotten the post to go viral. ↩

Thank you for your contributions Mark Shlick, Nikita Prokopov, and Alex Reichert! ↩
