title: Second set of twins a good distraction from injury - Maddison
description: Tottenham midfielder James Maddison says having five children aged four and under - including a second set of twins - helpfully distracted him from his ACL injury last season.
fullText:
The Football Interview will be available on BBC One at 12:45 every Saturday during the Premier League season, as well as on BBC iPlayer, BBC Football YouTube and the BBC Sport website and app.

The first episode of the new season, available on Saturday, 22 August, sees Kelly Somers sit down with Tottenham Hotspur's James Maddison.

Tottenham midfielder James Maddison said he and his partner have been "in the trenches" at home with five children aged four and under during a period when he was sidelined from football with a serious knee injury.

The 29-year-old missed most of the 2025-26 season because of the ruptured anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) he suffered last August.

During his recovery, Maddison's partner gave birth to their second set of twins. He described it as the "toughest year of his life" but credited his family for helping him get through.

"I needed that positive distraction of my partner being pregnant and having to be there for her and forget about myself, even though I was going through a traumatic experience through my knee," he told Kelly Somers.

Despite that, life has not been easy.

"A lot of nappies flying about, a lot of accidents at home, but it'll all be worth it," he said.

"We still love it. I wouldn't change it for the world."

Maddison said that because of his prolonged absence from football, his eldest son Leo actually assumed at one point that he had left Spurs.

"I missed a year of football, and a year in a child's life - from three and a half to four and a half - it's obviously massive," he said.

"He couldn't even remember over a year ago when he was at all the games.

"It would be nice for him to come to the games again and actually remember Dad playing instead of just Dad sat at home watching him with a machine on his knee."

Spurs struggled last season, securing survival on the final day and finishing just two points above the relegation zone. Maddison said it was tough not to be able to help out.

"We probably struggled a little bit for creativity and I'm watching the games thinking, 'what would I be doing there?'," he said.

Despite those tough experiences, the midfielder described how Italian head coach Roberto de Zerbi helped lift the mood at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after taking over in March.

"He's very clever. He's very tactical. He's obsessed with football, you can see that," said Maddison.

"But to be honest, when he first came in – in comparison to pre-season and what we're training now - he didn't want to make it too complicated. He just wanted us to get the love back for playing football."

One of the first things the Italian did, revealed Maddison, was to organise a team meal, where alcohol was allowed.

The 29-year-old described De Zerbi telling his team: "We're all going to be drinking alcohol, we're all going to be having a good night."

Maddison explained: "He wanted us to have a night where we all just relax.

"That feeling that we got made everyone feel more knitted together, straight away."

Another thing De Zerbi did early on in his tenure was to put Maddison on the bench.

"I was almost like, 'I'm not ready to play yet, boss'," the midfielder said.

"But he said no. He said I can come on the bench in my slippers if I want. He just wanted me around the group and he thought that would benefit the group. I took that as a massive compliment and just acted as if I was part of the bench, part of the team.

"I'm not saying that's the reason why, but we managed to steer clear of the danger, which was a good feeling."

The midfielder made his return against Leeds on 11 May, but he has not been risked in pre-season so far. Despite that, Maddison remains confident for the season ahead.

"I'm working so hard to try and be fully fit and available for the majority of the season," he said.

"I want just a fully fit, healthy season where I can just enjoy football. Because if I'm fully fit and I'm healthy, then I know what I'm capable of. And I know that I can affect games more than a lot of players in this league. So, let's just hope for that."

title: What Happened to Josh Jacobs? Latest on the Packers RB’s Legal Situation and Whether He’ll Be Suspended by NFL
description: Josh Jacobs entered Green Bay Packers training camp with two separate questions hanging over his 2026 season. One involves a groin injury.
fullText:
Josh Jacobs entered Green Bay Packers training camp with two separate questions hanging over his 2026 season. One involves a groin injury. The more serious one involves an unresolvedlegal matter and the possibility of NFL discipline.

No suspension has been announced yet, but Jacobs remains under review by the league after his May arrest, while the Brown County District Attorney's Office has not filed formal criminal charges.

Police responded to a disturbance complaint involving Jacobs on May 23 in Hobart, Wis. He wasarrested and booked into Brown County Jail on suspicion of battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, and intimidation of a victim.

Jacobs' attorneys said he "vehemently denies the allegations." The running back wasreleased from custody on May 27 after prosecutors said they were not prepared to make a formal charging decision and had requested additional investigation.

The case has remained unresolved. The Brown County District Attorney's Office said in late July that the investigation was "still open" and an update would be provided once a resolution was reached. Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst also described it as anongoing legal situation, with Green Bay and the NFL waiting for the process to play out.

That distinction is important. Jacobs was arrested, but as of Aug. 21, no formal criminal charges have been filed against him.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

A suspension remains possible, but it is not confirmed.

ESPN's Adam Schefterreported Aug. 11 that Jacobs' situation is "still under review" and remains a "pending situation" with the NFL. Schefter said discipline is still a potential option as the league works through several unresolved player cases before the regular season.

The NFL'sconduct policy allows discipline independent of the outcome of a criminal case. Its baseline punishment for a violation involving assault, battery, or domestic violence is six games without pay, although mitigating or aggravating circumstances can change the length.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Green Bay therefore cannot assume Jacobs will be available when it opens the season Sept. 13 at the Minnesota Vikings, according to theofficial schedule. The league has not announced a decision or timetable.

His potential absence would be substantial. Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 15 games last season while adding 282 receiving yards and another score. He posted a 76.5 PFN RB Impact score last season, ranking 16th among qualifying running backs.

For now, Jacobs remains eligible to participate when healthy. He is also working back from the separate groin injury that has limited him during camp.

The legal process and the NFL review are moving on different tracks. Until either produces a resolution, Green Bay's Week 1 backfield comes with an unusually large asterisk.

title: What Klay Thompson signing with Heat means for Lakers
description: Klay Thompson, who had been tied to the Lakers this summer, reached a buyout agreement with the Nuggets on Friday and plans to sign a two-year, $13 million deal with the...
fullText:
Klay Thompson, who had been tied to the Lakers this summer, reached a buyout agreement with the Nuggets on Friday and plans to sign a two-year, $13 million deal with the Heat.

What does that mean for the Purple and Gold?

Thompson was far from the perfect fit for the Lakers, even though the team very much needs to bolster its perimeter shooting and Thompson ranks fourth on the NBA's all-time 3-pointers made list.

The Lakers need a young and athletic wing, such as Jonathan Kuminga, to pair with Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. The Western Conference is young, fast and deep — with the Thunder and Spurs seemingly having an endless army of fresh legs at their disposal.

The 36-year-old Thompson no longer fits that bill, even though he helped the Warriors win four championships in eight years with his legendary sharpshooting. Last season, Thompson averaged 11.7 points on 39.3% shooting from the field and 38.3% from beyond the arc for the Mavericks, who failed to make the playoffs in Thompson's two seasons with the team amid health issues.

The Lakers pursued Thompson in free agency in 2024 before he ultimately decided to join the Mavericks. Thompson and Luka Doncic played 21 games together in Dallas before the Mavericks stunningly traded the superstar to the Lakers in February 2025, a deal that was a great blow for Thompson's title-winning hopes.

Thompson has deep ties to Los Angeles. His father, Mychal, won two championships with the Showtime Lakers in 1987 and 1988 and currently serves as the team's radio color analyst. And Thompson attended Rancho Margarita High and was a huge Kobe Bryant fan as a child.

But Thompson will now compete for his fifth ring in Miami alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

As for the Lakers, they'll continue their search for an athletic wing who could help them win their first title since 2020.

title: Josh McDaniels has ideal response as to whether Tom Brady helped Seahawks
description: Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels worked in New England for each of the six Super Bowls that Tom Brady won there.
fullText:
Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels worked in New England for each of the six Super Bowls that Tom Brady won there. As McDaniels tried to win a seventh against the Seahawks in February, Brady declared that he didn't have a "dog in the fight."

Since then, speculation has emerged that Brady, a Raiders owner, helped Seattle in its effort to beat New England. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel recently shrugged at that possibility, given that Brady was preparing to hire Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak.

McDaniels had a chance to chime in on Friday, during an appearance on WEEI in Boston.

Asked if he thinks Brady helped the Seahawks, McDaniels said, "I have no idea."

McDaniels then was asked whether it would bother him, if that had happened. Said McDaniels, "I wouldn't have a dog in that fight."

It's the ideal response, turning Brady's clunky throwaway line back at him.

Regardless of how current and former Patriots players and coaches may feel about Brady's neutrality, Patriots fans were and still are pissed off about it. With one comment, he went from being one of them to being an outsider — even though his statue is now parked outside Gillette Stadium.

It makes his anticipated return to Foxborough to call the Week 9 game between the Packers and the Patriots even more intriguing. How will he be received that day? Even if most fans cheer his return, it likely won't be universal among fans who feel betrayed by Brady's decision to not publicly support the Patriots — and the possibility that he privately helped the Seahawks win the game.

The fact that the issue came up during two separate Friday interviews on WEEI (one with McDaniels and one with linebacker Robert Spillane) shows that the locals haven't forgotten. Which surely means that many of them haven't forgiven.

title: ‘Worth Taking a Flyer On’ — NFL Reporter Lists Chiefs, Texans Among Landing Spots for 8-Time Pro Bowler
description: With less than a month remaining before the new season kicks off, the focus for many teams is on training camp and the preseason to make internal improvements to the roster. However, as injuries alter their roster dynamics, some might look to add more talent to their locker room.
fullText:
With less than a month remaining before the new season kicks off, the focus for many teams is on training camp and the preseason to make internal improvements to the roster. However, as injuries alter their roster dynamics, some might look to add more talent to their locker room.

For one analyst, the Kansas City Chiefs and the Houston Texans fall in that boat. The former, after barely making a move to improve their wide receiver corps, and the latter, after losing one of its potential starters for the season, could aim to add a veteran to their core.

Last season, both the Chiefs and the Texans were underwhelming offensively. Kansas City finished at number 13 on PFN's Offense Impact Metric, while Houston dropped all the way to number 21.

For both teams, some of those numbers could be attributed to injuries. For the Chiefs, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL near the end of the season, while both Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy missed significant chunks of the year.

The Texans, on the other hand, had C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins miss some games, while Tank Dell was out for the entire season. Neither team, though, has made any major upgrades to their passing game, as they expect improved health to carry them forward.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

But while the Texans have the star power, at least on paper, a torn ACL has sidelined Jayden Higgins for the entire season. Meanwhile, the Chiefs' receiving corps looks far from a unit that is poised to compete for a playoff spot.

As a result, Ryan Wilson of CBS Sports, who was making a case for Tyreek Hill to find his next team in the NFL, had those two squads near the top of the list. He believed that the eight-time Pro Bowler could be a needle mover for some team later down the line.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

"We very conceivably could see him not be on the field this season," Wilson said about Hill. "But he was just so incredibly dynamic before that terrible knee injury that you wonder, if a team gets desperate and we get into October, November, December, and you're down the stretch with Tyreek Hill, even at 65-70%, be worth taking a flyer on? I think the answer is yes."

And he even had a few specific teams in mind where the former Super Bowl champion could make the biggest impact.

"The Texans, they just lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL; they could certainly be in the running," Wilson added. "The Kansas City Chiefs' reunion will always be a talking point."

Wilson also floated the Los Angeles Chargers as the third potential landing spot for Hill, whose agentearlier today confirmed that the star wideout could possibly sign with a team closer to the playoffs.

It remains to be seen what the exact timeline for Hill's recovery from injury will be. But as Wilson detailed, there is a spot on multiple NFL teams for him if and when he returns to the field, even if in a diminished role compared to what he previously had.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: ESPN analyst makes one very bold claim about Ohio State this year
description: ESPN analyst EJ Manuel believes has gone on the record with an awfully bold claim about this year's Ohio State football team.
fullText:
There have only been two teams in the history of the Associated Press preseason poll (dating back to 1950) that have gone wire to wire as the No. 1 team in the country from the preseason to ultimately winning the national championship. As we enter the 2026 season, Ohio State becomes the next team with that opportunity.

Ohio State enters the season as the top-ranked team in the preseason AP Poll -- a ranking that no team really cares to have. It's the one at the end of the season that matters most. The Buckeyes were able to reach that pinnacle back in 2024 and are looking to make their way back to the top of the mountain this year.

Whether or not it's wire-to-wire is to be determined. But according to former Florida State quarterback and current college football analyst EJ Manuel, he believes Ohio State can do it this season.

"Well, my bold prediction is Julian Sayin, the Ohio State quarterback, will lead his team to a national title, wire-to-wire as the number one team in the country," Manuel said on ESPN's Get Up. "When reading this poll, think about some of the games they have on the road at Texas, at Iowa, at Indiana, at USC. I think Ohio State can win them all."

The Buckeyes, who not only play at Texas in Week 2, will be tested each and every week in the Big Ten. With one of the most difficult schedules in the country, four of Ohio State's five road games are going to be against preseason top-25 opponents. That's no easy task to come out of each week unscathed.

While Ohio State does have two Heisman Trophy contenders in Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, there is still one question that ESPN analyst Jordan Rodgers responded to Manuel's statement with.

"Here's my concern, and I agree with everything that EJ said about Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith. The offense is dynamic," Rodgers said. "They lost their three best players on defense. All who got drafted really high: Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles, Caleb Downs. Caleb Downs was the third of them. You don't just plug and play and replace guys like that. So I guess I think the offense can actually absolutely take them there. Can that defense reload the dynamic, all-world-type players they lost and get to the … national championship?"

Ohio State begins the season against Ball State -- which will also serve as Senior Day for the Buckeyes -- on September 5. Will the lessons Ryan Day learned a year ago and throughout his career help build this Ohio State team into a College Football Playoff national champion? Time will tell.

title: Patriots scouting report: Elijah Ponder is an explosive athlete on the edge
description: Previewing the Patriots edge defender heading into his second NFL season.
fullText:
The New England Patriots entered the 2025 NFL Draft facing significant questions at multiple positions, including the defensive edge. However, their investments were relatively minimal. In fact, their best contributions from a rookie edge last season came not from a draft pick but an undrafted free agent.

Heading into his second season in the league, Elijah Ponder now is looking ready to play an even more prominent role.

Position: Defensive edge/Outside linebacker

Opening day age: 24 (8/24/2002)

Measurements: 6'2 7/8", 261 lbs, 10 1/8" hand size, 33 1/8" arm length, 80" wingspan, 4.63s 40-yard dash, 6.99s 3-cone drill, 4.28s short shuttle, 41" vertical jump, 11'0" broad jump, 22 bench press reps, 9.87 Relative Athletic Score

NFL:New England Patriots (2025-) | College: Cal Poly (2020-24)

A multi-sport athlete at Bishop Amat High School in La Puente, CA, Ponder received some FCS interest as a two-star outside linebacker recruit. Ultimately, however, he decided to head for the FBS and joined Cal Poly. In five seasons with the Mustangs, he saw action in 47 games with 42 starts. He also registered 26.5 sacks and 43.5 tackles for loss, and was named All-Big Sky in all four of his non-redshirt campaigns (first team 2023, 2024; honorable mention 2021, 2022).

Despite his college success, Ponder did not hear his name called in the 2025 NFL Draft. He joined the Patriots as an undrafted free agent afterwards and appeared in 19 games as a rookie with four sacks and three fumble recoveries.

Strengths: Checking in at 6-foot-3 and 261 pounds, Ponder offers good size on the defensive edge. He combines it with an intriguing athletic skillset; his explosivity, agility and speed are rare, and he looks the part on the field as well. He is quick to attack the pocket and has the burst to challenge blockers' leverage and balance early into a rep, plays with active hands, and can properly bend the corner around the edge. He also has good spatial awareness, which in turn allows him to locate the football effectively even in traffic, and the range to be a factor in pursuit.

Weaknesses: Ponder moves as well as any outside linebacker in football, but he fails to consistently look the part on the field. His game speed and timed speed do not always align, in parts because he is still a developing player from a technical and processing perspective. He also lacks ideal length and is not the most powerful player at the point of attack. He furthermore is a pass-first player whose contributions against the run have been limited so far. When he has been asked to play the run, he has failed to consistently set the edge and contain runs to the inside.

Stats: 19 games (0 starts) | 314 defensive snaps (24.5%), 287 special teams snaps (52.4%) | 17 tackles, 1 missed tackle (5.6%), 4 TFLs, 2 FRs | 24 QB pressures (4 sacks, 3 hits, 17 hurries) | 11 special teams tackles, 3 missed tackles (21.4%), 1 FR | 3 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting)

Season recap: Despite his small-school status, Ponder was invited to both the Hula Bowl and the East-West Shrine Bowl heading toward the draft. As noted above, however, he was not selected in any of the seven rounds and had to navigate the free agency waters before finding a home in the NFL. The journey, however, was a rather short one: he joined the Patriots as one of their first-wave UDFA signings.

While that meant he started out buried on the depth chart, Ponder steadily climbed his way up the ranks. Strong showings in training camp and preseason ultimately allowed him to join wide receiver Efton Chism as the only two undrafted rookies to make New England's initial 53-man roster. Even though he lacked pedigree, he remained there throughout the sesaon.

Early on, Ponder was mostly a special teamer. Even as his defensive role evolved, he kept seeing regular action as a four-unit contributor in the kicking game to eventually finish sixth among his teammates in snaps and third in tackles.

On defense, meanwhile, he saw a handful of snaps over the first half of the season. However, with starting edge Harold Landry starting to deal with nagging injury woes, he managed to grow his role: from Week 12 on, when Landry's issues started impacting his availability, Ponder was on the field for roughly 36.8% of snaps. Those snaps came predominately in the passing game, with early-down duties falling on fellow edge Anfernee Jennings.

In that relatively specialized role, Ponder delivered some good performances. In fact, his affinity for finding the football and recovering fumbles — his three FRs were tied for the team lead in 2025 — turned out crucial: he helped set up the only touchdown of the Patriots' AFC Championship win in Denver (and in fact would have scored himself on the play if not for a bad call by the officials).

BALL WAS OUT – GOING THE OTHER WAY‼️

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/swmdTx0TYV

All in all, Ponder had a very good first season in the NFL. It may not have started as he had hoped by not hearing his name called in the draft, but his effort and playmaking abilities earned him his way onto the Patriots' roster. Once there, he showed that he belonged.

Position: Outside linebacker | Ability: Depth player/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2027 (2028 RFA)

What will be his role? Ponder has worked as an outside linebacker throughout training camp so far, and in fact has been a regular as the starter opposite Dre'Mont Jones. While Harold Landry's eventual return from the physically unable to perform list will shake things up, Ponder currently projects as a rotational third or fourth option at the position as well as a key special teamer.

What is his growth potential? From an athletic perspective, Ponder's ceiling is sky-high. There are, however, questions about how far he can actually still climb and whether he can become more than a depth piece. If he can clean up his own personal operation, there is no reason to believe that he can't be a serviceable third or fourth member in an edge room.

Does he have positional versatility? Defensively, Ponder's versatility is somewhat limited; he is mostly a pass rusher at this point in his development. However, the game's third phase is a different story. On special teams, he played at least 45 snaps on each of the core four units (kickoff return, kickoff coverage, punt return, punt coverage) and there is no reason to believe he can't play a similar role in 2026.

What is his salary cap situation? Arriving via a standard three-year UDFA deal last offseason, Ponder is carrying a $1.01 million cap number into the coming season. That number consists almost entirely of his $1.005 million base salary as well as a $5,000 signing bonus proration. That bonus is the only part of the deal guaranteed, which means that it also is currently his only trace in New England's books under the NFL's Top 51 role.

How safe is his roster spot? Heading into the second preseason game, anything but Ponder making the 53-man roster would be a surprise. He has been the top option to replace Harold Landry in the lineup, after all, and has had some positive moments throughout training camp. Add his special teams role and he should be expected on the active team come the fall.

Summary: Ponder is one of those players who won't be able to make the game-changing plays or demand special attention on a weekly basis. That said, he is still immensely valuable to the operation but defensively and in the kicking game.

What do you think about Elijah Ponder heading into the 2026 season? Will he increase his role? Or will he cede snaps to rookie Gabe Jacas? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts with the rest of the community.

title: Can Tadej Pogacar Become Ninth Rider In History To Win All Three Grand Tours At Least Once?
description: Tadej Pogacar is aiming to become the ninth rider in history to win all three Grand Tours at least one time. He'll have his chance at La Vuelta 2026.
fullText:
Tadej Pogačar is perhaps the greatest to ever do it, but there is one thing missing from his extensive list of accomplishments: a win at the Vuelta a España.

The six-time Grand Tour champion - five at the Tour de France and one the Giro d'Italia - will look to complete the collection with a victory at La Vuelta 2026, which gets underway Aug. 22 and will run through Sept. 13.

Pogačar is aiming to become the ninth rider in history to win all three Grand Tours at least one time each, and reaching that goal will require outlasting some of the best riders in the world over 21 challenging stages.

Fans in Canada can watch all of the action, live and on demand, on FloBikes and the FloSports app.

Vuelta a España 2026 To Start In Monaco And Finish In Granada

Tadej Pogačar To Race The Vuelta a España 2026

5 Reasons Cycling Fans Need To Watch The 2026 Vuelta a España

The Vuelta a España is the third Grand Tour of the cycling season. It first was held in 1935 and has been contested every year since 1955.

This year marks the 81st edition of La Vuelta, but only the second start for Pogačar, who made it the first Grand Tour of his career when he debuted in 2019.

The following season, his summertime focus turned to the Tour de France, and he has won that race in five of the seven years he has participated (2020, 2021, 2024, 2025, 2026). The other two times, he was the runner-up to Jonas Vingegaard (2022, 2023).

In 2024, Pogačar became the first rider since 1998 to win the Giro d'Italia and Tour de France in the same year, and he now can become the latest to complete the TDF-La Vuelta double.

Can Pogačar add to his growing legacy with a win at La Vuelta 2026?

As it turned out, yes, Jonas Vingegaard was the man to beat at the Vuelta a España in 2025.

He won three stages on the way to his first GC title at La Vuelta, which was affected in multiple stages by pro-Palestinian protests. He finished the 21 days of racing 1 minute, 16 seconds ahead of João Almeida, who won two stages of his own.

Despite continued success during his career, Vingegaard also has suffered some pretty serious injuries, including a high-speed crash in the Tour of the Basque Country in 2024 that resulted in a broken collarbone, broken ribs and a punctured lung.

He's now recovering from a crash and broken collarbone during the 2026 Tour de France that likely will see him miss the chance to defend his title at the Vuelta a España.

After winning La Vuelta last summer, Vingegaard was able to continue his strong form at the 2025 Giro d'Italia, where he won the GC crown and became the eighth rider in history to win all three Grand Tours at least once.

At the Vuelta a España in 2024, Slovenia's Primoz Roglic won for a record-equaling fourth career victory at the storied race.

The former ski jumper has been plagued by crashes and injuries, including two significant ones in 2024, but he continues to persevere and managed to land himself among the year's most memorable moments with wins at the 2024 Critérium du Dauphiné and La Vuelta.

He won the Vuelta a España in 2019, 2020 and 2021 and joined Spain's Roberto Heras as the event's only four-time champions (2000, 2003, 2004, 2005).

title: Sergio Garcia’s Masters meltdown reportedly impetus for Saudi’s PIF to pull LIV funding
description: If Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), was looking for a reason to pull its money out of the LIV Golf tour, he reportedly found it in Sergio Garcia’s outburst at the Masters in April. That’s the claim in Friday’s edition of The Financial Times. “In April, as LIV golfers floundered…
fullText:
If Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), was looking for a reason to pull its money out of the LIV Golf tour, he reportedly found it in Sergio Garcia's outburst at the Masters in April.

That's the claim in Friday's edition of The Financial Times.

"In April, as LIV golfers floundered at the Masters, golf's most prestigious tournament, Spanish star Sergio Garcia damaged the Augusta National course during a fit of rage in the final round," read the Times. "People familiar with the matter say Rumayyan's embarrassment at the sequence of events helped lead to his decision to pull the plug on PIF's financing of the rival tour, as the fund focuses more on its huge domestic commitments in the kingdom."

Now, one's first thought is likely that many factors led the PIF to pull its funding from LIV, which has consistently lost money amid poor ratings and bad PR since its brief moment in the sun. However, when you look at the timing of everything, it kinda checks out.

A whole series of events from Sergio Garcia earlier on Sunday at the Masters

Slams his driver in frustration
 Breaks his driver against a cooler
 Carries Jon Rahm’s bag while Rahm’s caddie tends to a bunker pic.twitter.com/he09pvWuv8

Garcia's meltdown, which included him slamming his driver in frustration, tearing out chunks of grass, and breaking it against a cooler, took place on Sunday, April 12, the final day of the 2026 Masters.

Rumayyan, whose desire to become a member of Augusta National has been well documented, was watching and was presumably not pleased with the behavior.

Now, Joel Beall of Golf Digest did note that internal discussion about PIF pulling funding from LIV were already underway before Garcia had a temper tantrum in Augusta, so all of the blame can't be laid at the golfer's feet. However, it does sound as though the incident, which reflected poorly on both Garcia and LIV, doused some lighter fluid on the wood pile, so to speak.

title: Yankees prospects: Hudson Valley sees ‘a lot of Ben Rice’ in converted catcher
description: Here are scouting reports on position players of the Yankees' High A farm club, the Hudson Valley Renegades, from manager Aaron Bossi.
fullText:
LAKEWOOD, N.J. — It's been slim pickings this year for Yankees position player prospects for the High-A Hudson Valley Renegades and they lost three of their best ones this month, all infielders.

First, Kaeden Kent went to the Giants in a trade on Aug. 3 then two players were promoted to the Double-A Somerset Patriots, Roderick Arias on Aug. 4 and Core Jackson on Aug. 11.

That left Hudson Valley with two Yankees position player prospects ranked among their top 30 by MLB Pipeline — and one of them, Wilson Rodriguez, is done for the year with a thumb injury.

The over/under for Wednesday's AL East clash between the Yankees and the Orioles is set at 9 total runs on BetMGM. Our comprehensive BetMGM Sportsbook review provides an in-depth guide on how to use their app.

The Renegades do have Eric Genther, a left-handed hitter who switched from left field to catcher this year. Opponents are running like crazy on him, but his coaching staff is seeing steady progress.

The Renegades have an under the radar prospect who isn't on any of their top 30 rankings. Jackson Lovich was leading the Florida State League in homers when he was promoted to High A on July 28 and he's off to a great start with Hudson Valley, batting .343 in six games counting his 1-for-4 with a three-run homer in Tuesday night's 10-5 win at Jersey Shore.

Here are scouting reports on the Renegades' top three hitting prospects from manager Aaron Bossi:

Acquired: Signed as undrafted free agent on July 16, 2025.

2026 hitting stats: Hudson Valley (High A), 267 average, 352 AB, 60 runs, 94 hits, 19 doubles, 1 triple, 12 HR, 57 RBI, 7 SB, 1 CS, 57 BB, 82 K, .830 OPS, 104 games.

2026 fielding stats: Hudson Valley (High A), 14 errors, 7 passed balls, 169 steals allowed, 19 CS in 57 games (57 starts) at catcher.

Career hitting stats: .266 average, 395 AB, 70 runs, 105 hits, 23 doubles, 1 triple, 13 HR, 64 RBI, 9 SB, 1 CS, 67 BB, 89 K, .835 OPS, 121 games in 2 seasons (2025-26).

Prospect ranking: MLB Pipeline, Not in top 30; Baseball America, No. 27.

The skinny: Switched to catching this season after playing outfield for Low A Tampa in 2025 (11 games LF, 5 games RF). … Had a two-hit, four-RBI game in a Monday night win at Jersey Shore. … Batting .276 with 12 homers against right-handed pitching and .217 with no homers versus lefties. … 18.6 strikeout percentage, 13.1 walk percentage. … Drexel Hill, Pa. native was a four-year starter at Rhode Island and hit .367 as a senior. … Ranks in top five in Rhode Island's career leaders for homers, RBI, doubles and walks. … Mother played basketball at Rider.

Manager Aaron Bossi's take: "We told Eric right after our A ball season last year that we were moving him to catcher. He caught in 2022 at Rhode Island for a few games, but it wasn't much at all. We made the change because we saw the offensive profile and thought this could maximize Eric's value. That transition from outfield was intriguing because he had a good arm out there. So now it's about moving like a catcher, shortening up the release, quickening up the feet. While the stolen bases stat doesn't look great right now, we are seeing real-time gains in how quickly he's been able to release the ball and how accurately he's able to deliver it to the base. Eric is noticeably better each time he goes out there. He's in control of the game. In his first couple starts, the game was moving really fast and he was exposed to some things. The blocking and the pitch receiving have grown so much and so fast to a very serviceable level right now. My messaging to Eric is he's gonna be a big-league catcher. When he's hitting, it's consistent bat to ball and his ability to impact it hard consistently. I look at Eric, I see a lot of Ben Rice. He's a guy who constantly gets his barrel to the ball. He hits for a high slug because he's able to consistently elevate the ball. He's still continuing to adjust and build his offensive profile. That's certainly not complete yet, which makes you even more excited about him because it is so good right now."

Age: 21 (22 on Sept. 10, 2026).

Acquired: 2023 draft, 17th round (Academia Presbiteriana High School; Carolina, Puerto Rico). $150,000 signing bonus.

2026 hitting stats: Hudson Valley (High A), .259 average, 293 AB, 55 runs, 76 hits, 15 doubles, 5 triples, 8 HR, 43 RBI, 20 SB, 5 CS, 43 BB, 58 K, .806 OPS, 84 games.

2026 fielding stats: Hudson Valley (High A), 2 errors, 3 assists, .963 fielding percentage in 43 games (42 starts) in right field; 2 errors, 1 assist, .967 fielding percentage, 35 games (35 starts) in left field; 0 errors, 1 assist, 1.000 fielding percentage in 7 games (7 starts) in center field.

Career hitting stats: .246 average, 544 AB, 89 runs, 134 hits, 26 doubles, 7 triples, 14 HR, 79 RBI, 32 SB, 8 CS, 79 BB, 98 K, .760 OPS, 163 games.

Prospect ranking: MLB Pipeline, No. 24; Baseball America, Not in top 30.

MLB Pipeline tool grades (20/80 scale): Hit 45; Power 50; Run 55; Arm 50; Overall 40.

The skinny: Rodriguez had season-ending surgery after dislocating a thumb sliding into second base in a July 19 game at Brooklyn. … His 15.9 walk percentage was up from 11.9 in 2025, but his 19.8 strikeout percentage jumped from 17.6 in 2025.

Manager Aaron Bossi's take: "Wilson is an extremely passionate player. I think of him as a glue guy. He speaks both languages, English and Spanish, and really brings the team together. He goes out wanting to win every single day. It's really awesome to see that in the minor leagues. I saw a lot of progress from Wilson this season. He's slowed the game down so much defensively and on the bases. That helped his decision making on when to steal and which jumps to take and to trust. Defensively, he's played a lot of left and right field, but we started giving him center field games right before he unfortunately went down. He's got the athleticism to really cover some ground. He's got a really strong left-handed arm."

Acquired: 2025 draft, 16th round (Missouri). $150,000 signing bonus.

2026 hitting stats: Hudson Valley (High A), .343 average, 67 AB, 15 runs, 23 hits, 1 triple, 3 HR, 19 RBI, 10 SB, 1 CS, 7 BB, 27 K, .907 OPS, 6 games. Tampa (Low A), .275 average, 320 AB, 59 runs, 88 hits, 17 doubles, 2 triples, 18 HR, 61 RBI, 21 SB, 7 CS, 36 BB, 101 K, .859 OPS, 78 games.

2026 fielding stats: 16 errors, .970 fielding percentage, 45 games (45 starts) at shortstop; 7 errors, .939 fielding percentage, 34 games (34 starts) at 3rd base; 0 errors, 1.000 fielding percentage in 5 games (5 starts) in center field.

Career hitting stats: .306 average, 409 AB, 83 runs, 125 hits, 21 doubles, 5 triples, 21 HR, 89 RBI, 34 SB, 8 CS, 47 BB, 131 K, .912 OPS, 101 games.

Prospect ranking: MLB Pipeline, not in top 30; Baseball America, Not in top 30.

The skinny: Overland Park, Kansas native was the Mets' 19th-round draft pick in 2022, but opted for college. … Younger brother Eli Lovich is an outfielder for the Cubs' High-A Myrtle Beach affiliate after being drafted in the 11th round in 2024. … Scouts are impressed with Lovich's raw power and bat speed. … Debuted as a pro last season by hitting .636 (14-for-22) with nine RBI in six games with Low A Tampa. … In college hit .311 with 47 homers, 94 RBI in 116 games across three seasons with Missouri (2023-25).

Manager Aaron Bossi's take: "If Jackson's not on our prospect list, I would absolutely be looking out for him because he's so sharp in middle of your infield and now he's showing the athleticism to do it in the outfield as well. I think about his baseball IQ. I think about how engaged he is with every situation in the game, on the bases and on defense. He has a super sharp baseball mind and a lot of pop in that bat. He absolutely could stay at shortstop, but we're starting to roll him out center field games and he's so accepting. He's team centered and so passionate about the game."

title: Rams Land 3 Players on NFL’s Top 10 List
description: The Los Angeles Rams boast not one, not two but three of the NFL's top 10 players. The post Rams Land 3 Players on NFL’s Top 10 List appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams are facing monumental expectations this year due to their near-miss last season and stacked roster, so it's no surprise the NFL ranked multiple Rams as being among the best in the league.

That said, the number of top-tier players they have is hard to wrap your head around.

Perhaps the easiest way to describe it is this: Of the top 10 players at any position in football, three of them are Rams. No other team has more than one.

The NFL, when revealing who's in their top 10 ranking, included quarterback Matthew Stafford, the reigning MVP; wide receiver Puka Nacua and defensive end Myles Garrett.

Exactly where they fall in that top 10 hasn't been released — that comes next week — but it's still impressive that the team has multiple players ranked that highly in the first place.

Stafford is one of two QBs on the list, Nacua is one of two wide receivers and Garrett is one of two pass rushers, showing just how stiff the competition is for this type of honor.

With those stars and other key contributors like Davante Adams, Kyren Williams and Trent McDuffie, the Rams and coach Sean McVay have a very real shot at a title this season.

Coincidentally, that championship game, Super Bowl LXI, is at the Rams' house, SoFi Stadium in Inglewood.

And the last time the Rams won the Super Bowl in 2022, that game also was played at SoFi Stadium.

Whether it is a matter of happenstance or something just meant to be, the cards are certainly lining up for a Rams run at the title in 2026.

Do you think we'll see them at SoFi Stadium come Feb. 14, 2027?

title: Intercepted? Jets notch first INT in 364 days during preseason game vs. Steelers
description: The Jets haven't intercepted anything, especially a football, in a long time. That drought finally came to an end in Week 2 of the preseason.
fullText:
What a difference a year makes. Well, almost a year.

For the first time in 364 days, the New York Jets have intercepted a pass. No, not throw an interception. That was something they did 13 times during the regular season and 2026 starting quarterback, Geno Smith, did 17 times alone while with the Las Vegas Raiders. This was different.

A Jets defender ended the interception drought – albeit unofficially – in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason.

Don't believe us? Take a look with your own eyes:

OUR BALL

📺: #NYJvsPIT on @NFLonCBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/QieWSkBBxl

From just inside the 15-yard line, Will Howard dropped back to pass early in the second quarter. Rather than find his receiver, he found Andre Cisco, the Jets safety.

It marked the team's first interception in a game of any kind since Aug. 22, 2025, against the Philadelphia Eagles. That came in the first quarter when the Eagles' Kyle McCord was picked off by Malachi Moore.

Turns out, the turnovers come in bunches: Samuel Womack picked off Howard for a second time in the second quarter.

anotha one

📺: #NYJvsPIT on @NFLonCBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/xyK3izLvqL

The Jets famously became the only team in NFL history, since the league started tracking interceptions in 1933, to go through a full season without recording one.

They'll need to find one in the regular season to avoid a repeat of 2025, but the team can at least celebrate being on the right side of that turnover for the first time in a long time.

title: Samantha Busch full speech from emotional Kyle Busch Invitational
description: Ahead of the Kyle Busch Invitational at Bowman Gray Stadium, Samantha Busch stood beside her son Brexton and offered some heartfelt words on the grid
fullText:
Featuring Legends cars and Bandoleros, dozens of drivers took part in the Kyle Busch Invitational at Bowman Gray Stadium on Friday.

KB's 11-year-old son Brexton was among those competing, and before the green flag flew, and Kyle's wife Samantha gave a remarkable speech for all those gathered at the historic short track.

Here is the full transcript of Samantha Busch's five-minute speech, as well as a video of the incredible moment:

Watch Samantha Busch's message to fans ahead of the main events in the Kyle Busch Invitational at Bowman Gray Stadium.

📺 NASCAR Channel & @FloRacing pic.twitter.com/cg2Zri365G

"First, I simply want to say thank you to each and every one of you here tonight. These past few months have been the hardest of our lives and I don't think I'll ever be able to fully explain the love and support from all of you and what it has meant to myself, Brexton, Lennix, and our entire family.

"This race was something Kyle really wanted to put together. The excitement in his voice and the twinkle in his eyes when he was telling me about texting Ben, trying to make it happen, was like watching a kid on Christmas. He loved this place. It's history and the energy here, but more than anything, Kyle loved grassroots racing.

"It was where his love for this sport began and no matter how far his career took him, he never lost that. He believed in giving young racers a place to learn, compete, and dream big and fall in love with this sport the same way that he did. And for me, having Brexton out here racing tonight makes it even more emotional.

"Racing was such a special bond between Kyle and Brexton. Kyle loved being your dad more than anything and he loved getting to share this sport with him. Watching Brexton continue chasing his dreams without his dad beside him is absolutely heartbreaking. 
But I am so grateful for all the people that surround us that love Kyle. Tonight is also incredibly special because this event supports the Bundle of Joy Fund. Kyle and I started the Bundle of Joy Fund from one of the hardest chapters in our own lives.

"We spent almost a decade trying to complete our family. We battled infertility, miscarriages, and IVF and it was extremely difficult, but we knew how fortunate we were to be able to keep trying. We knew we wanted to give that same hope to other couples desperately praying for a family of their own.

"Fatherhood changed Kyle in the most beautiful ways and it was clear to see how much this mission meant to him. Knowing that something we built together will continue helping families grow by bringing babies into this world for years to come is the most beautiful piece of Kyle's legacy that we get to carry forward. And when I think about Kyle's legacy, I know it doesn't just belong to our family.

"So much of it lives right here in this racing community and with all of you that have supported him, cheered for him, and loved him throughout his entire career. Kyle was a racer to his core, but he knew the sport was nothing without you fans. You all showed up for him, you loved on him, and you are loving on us when we need you the most. 
And I am so appreciative. So thank you for being here. Thank you for loving Kyle.

"Thank you for cheering for Brexton and Lennix ... Sorry (wipes tears away). Every time you tell a Kyle story, carry a piece of who he was into your own life, you help keep his legacy alive.

"Work hard, never stop trying to be your best, and stay true to who you are. Those are the things that Kyle lived every day, and I hope that those are the pieces of him that continue to live on in all of us. Racing will never be the same without him.

"Our lives will never be the same without him. But I know Kyle's love for this sport, his impact on it, and the legacy he left behind, and will continue to do so through all of us. So tonight, let's do exactly what Kyle had wanted.

title: Ohio State basketball adds Argentine forward to 2026-27 roster
description: The Ohio State basketball team added a seasoned Argentine forward to cap a busy offseason and in reworking its 2026-27 roster.
fullText:
It appears the 2026-27 Ohio State basketball roster is still morphing. Lee Aaliya, a 6-foot-9, 225-pound forward from Argentina, will bring professional experience to head coach Jake Diebler's roster. The 21-year-old has played overseas for the last five years, most recently for UCAM Murcia in Spain's Liga ACB, which is considered one of the top leagues internationally.

"Lee is an energetic big who I am excited to have join our Buckeye family," Diebler said in a release. "His experience, athleticism, and physicality make him a valuable addition to our program."

Aaliya averaged 18.4 points and 9.6 rebounds while shooting nearly 60% from the field for UCAM Murcia's top team this past season. He helped Atenas de Cordoba reach the Final Four of the South American Basketball Champions League the year prior.

Aaliya's eligibility remains up in the air with the NCAA. While he is permitted to practice, he will have to wait for an official decision before he suits up for an actual game, so the end of this story is still being written at a time when college sports are -- shall we say -- ever-changing and oh so unpredictable.

With Aaliya in the fold, the Ohio State roster has a full set of 15 players for the upcoming season. The roster has gone through a major revision this offseason, and now Jake Diebler knows exactly who will help him attempt to get back to the top of the Big Ten.

title: Good Sports: Merced teens leave home to pursue pro soccer dreams
description: Leaving home to follow a dream. That's what both Immanuel Ewing and Jorge Salmeron did at just 13 and 14 years old. The boys signed MLS Next Pro contracts with Crew 2.
fullText:
Leaving home to follow a dream.

"At first, it was hard leaving my family," says Jorge Salmeron.

That's what both Immanuel Ewing and Jorge Salmeron did at just 13 and 14 years old.

"It's super hard, especially the first year," Ewing said.

"Leaving your family behind, your siblings behind, but he's definitely willing to make that sacrifice and work hard for it," says Mariana Rivera, Ewing's mother.

Both Immanuel and Jorge grew up playing soccer in Merced with Albion SC.

To reach their goal of the pros, the two made a sacrifice: leave home and join an MLS developmental academy.

"We see them competing at the highest level," says Albion SC Coach Rafael Valencia. "You see it in the intensity they bring in practice."

The Merced kids found their way to Columbus, Ohio, earning a spot with the Columbus Crew Academy.

Each has made appearances with Crew 2, the last step before becoming a pro.

In the inaugural MLS Next Cup, Immanuel won the MVP award for the U-19 championship.

"It's definitely something I didn't think I would end up getting," he said. "I never thought I would be able to achieve something like that."

Now, both Immanuel and Jorge are making more than just an appearance.

The boys signed MLS Next Pro contracts with Crew 2.

"It's just something you've been wanting for your whole life," Jorge said.

The Crew franchise gains two Valley natives after losing one in July.

Fresno native Max Arfsten was picked by the Crew in the 2023 MLS SuperDraft, won an MLS Cup with the team before being named to the U-S men's national team roster and debuting in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Max is on his way to the English Championship side with Middlesbrough FC, passing the reins to Immanuel and Jorge to represent the Valley here in the States.

"All the hard work is finally paying off," Jorge said. "It's just a small step to keep pushing forward."

"For all the little kids out here, kind of just give them something to look up to," Immanuel said. "Show them that there's stuff outside of Merced. It's not just this small town. You can do whatever you put your mind to."

title: Analyst confident in Ian Machado Garry's title future after UFC 330 loss
description: One prominent UFC analyst and commentator "can confidently say" Ian Machado Garry will eventually hold welterweight gold.
fullText:
Michael Chiesa remains bullish on Ian Machado Garry's upside despite falling short in his first bid at gold.

Machado Garry (17-2 MMA, 10-2 UFC) suffered a unanimous decision loss to Islam Makhachev (29-1 MMA, 18-1 UFC) in their UFC 330 welterweight title fight this month, but the Irishman was more competitive than many pundits and the oddsmakers indicated.

Although Machado Garry did not get the belt at UFC 330, retired welterweight standout turned UFC analyst and commentator Chiesa still saw flashes of brilliance. If Machado Garry can build on those going forward, it could lead him to the ultimate prize.

"Ian Garry's stock to me still goes up," Chiesa told MMA Junkie. "I don't think his stock goes down at all. There are people that definitely had him picked to win, and he didn't fight a bad fight. But he could have fought better. But his stock still goes up. He was able to defend takedowns. He made it really hard for Islam. He made Islam have to ditch MMA and focus on wrestling to get through the late rounds of that fight.

"Ian's stock still goes up. I can confidently say there is a world where he has a world title someday. Especially given how young he is. 28 years old. He's got a lot of time to win a title."

UFC CEO Dana White sparked a key post-fight narrative around Machado Garry at UFC 330 when he criticized a lack of "killer instinct" shown against Makhachev. The champ echoed that sentiment and said Machado Garry displayed "too much respect."

Chiesa can stand behind that perspective as someone who stepped into the octagon 22 times and never showed mid-fight gestures of appreciation to his opponent, and agrees it might have prevented Machado Garry for greater success at UFC 330.

"There is a certain limit, especially when you did lose," Chiesa said. "It's like, OK, you're down 3-0. You've got to get on the gas. It's time to stop being friends, and you've got to take this guy's head off. Ian is out to try to knock you out, but you can save the hugging and all that crap from before the fight for after the fight. But for 15 to 25 minutes, you've got to be locked in trying to take someone's head off."

To hear more Chiesa, check out his complete appearance on "The Bohnfire" podcast with MMA Junkie senior reporter Mike Bohn above.

title: New York Times loses defamation suit, ordered to pay $9.25M to former Alabama basketball player
description: An Alabama jury awarded Kai Spears $9.25 million in damages after finding The New York Times defamed the former University of Alabama basketball player.
fullText:
The New York Times was defeated in a defamation lawsuit Thursday brought by a former college basketball player and ordered to pay millions in damages.

An Alabama jury ruled the Times defamed Kai Spears, then an 18-year-old freshman walk-on basketball player for the University of Alabama's Crimson Tide, who was swept up in a 2023 report linking him to a fatal shooting.

After a nine-day trial, the eight-person jury determined that Spears was owed $9.25 million in damages.

Israeli Pm Netanyahu Initiating Defamation Lawsuit Against New York Times Over Controversial 'Dog Rape' Story

Spears was mentioned in the March 2023 report authored by New York Times sportswriter Billy Witz. Spears was falsely identified as being a passenger in the car at the site of a January 2023 shooting that resulted in the death of 23-year-old Jamea Harris.

The Times issued a lengthy editor's note to the report in June 2023, but only after Spears filed the defamation lawsuit at the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama.

"The original version of this article, published March 15, misidentified the person who was in the car with [Crimson Tide star player] Brandon Miller when the shooting occurred," the note began.

"Based on information from a person familiar with the case, the article erroneously identified that person as Kai Spears, a freshman basketball player. After the article was initially published, Alabama's athletic director and Spears's father denied that Spears was present. The Times included those responses and reviewed its reporting, but did not conclude that any other change to the article was warranted at that time.

"On Wednesday, Spears filed a defamation suit against The Times that included new details about the incident. Based on that information, editors assigned further reporting, which determined that the other person at the scene was not Spears but Cooper Lee, a student manager for the team. The Times regrets the error in the initial report."

Jury Finds Cnn Committed Defamation Against Navy Veteran, Settlement Reached In Punitive Damages

Witz, who began reporting for The Times in 2008, relied on one anonymous source who claimed Spears was at the site of the shooting. Witz testified the source was a "high-level person, professional."

"I think the way I was looking at it, Source A, by their job title and by virtue of their access to the transcript, videos and impound photos, was somebody who knew a lot about this case," Witz said, according to a report from The Tuscaloosa Patch.

"In my mind, the story had a focus, and this tragedy, as bad as it was, could have been much worse."

A separate anonymous source had told Witz, "I can tell you it's a White guy on the basketball team, I just don't remember his name," according to Witz's testimony.

According to The Patch, Witz ultimately conceded from the witness stand, "Yes, [the story] had a mistake, no question."

Reporter Who Exited Cnn After Being At Center Of Costly Defamation Trial Lands At Al Jazeera English

The Times noted in its own report about the verdict that it had not lost a defamation lawsuit brought in the United States over one of its articles in more than 50 years.

"We're disappointed the jury found The Times liable for an honest mistake," a Times spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "We thank the jury for its service, but believe the verdict and award of damages are contrary to law and not supported by the evidence. We are reviewing our legal options."

Spears' legal team did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: 'We are devastated' - Nigerian villagers bury bodies after overloaded boat capsizes
description: The overloaded boat was taking people, including many children, to farms to harvest rice.
fullText:
At least 48 people have died in Nigeria after an overloaded boat with an estimated 70 passengers capsized on a river in a remote area of north-western Sokoto state.

"We are devastated at the moment," Hussaini Shehu, a resident of Gorau village, told the BBC, explaining that the accident had happened on Thursday morning as people were heading out to their rice farms along the banks of the river.

Bashir Usman Gorau, a lawmaker the area, told the BBC that many of the victims were children.

In farming communities, children often accompany their parents to farms to help with agricultural activities - and at the moment the community is harvesting rice.

Why do boat disasters keep happening in Nigeria?

The authorities say search and rescue efforts are continuing as people are still missing - and teams worked through the night.

The remote location, poor access and unreliable mobile phone coverage has made it difficult to get information.

"There are over 70 people in the boat and l0 have been rescued," Shehu said.

Gorau said the wooden vessel had been overloaded but had also developed a leak "through which water gushed in".

A team from Nigeria's emergency management agency (Nema) has reached the area.

But Shehu said the security services had not been able to get to them as an armed group had been active nearby on Thursday.

The BBC has contacted the police for comment.

Heavily armed criminal gangs - which loot and kidnap for ransom - operate across parts of north-west and north-central Nigeria. The insecurity makes accessing remote areas difficult and has forced lots of communities to abandon their homes.

A militant jihadist group called Lakurawa has also been active in Sokoto and neighbouring Kebbi state.

Last December, US President Donald Trump and the Nigerian government launched airstrikes in Sokoto, saying they were targeting Islamic State militants. IS has not linked itself to Lakurawa as it has done with other groups in the region that it backs.

Boat accidents are common in Nigeria, with overcrowding, poorly maintained boats and weak enforcement of safety rules often blamed for deaths. At least five people drowned when a boat overturned in Jigawa state last month.

In January, at least 26 people drowned when a boat carrying farmers and fishermen from Jigawa to Yobe state capsized.

And in December 2024, 54 bodies were recovered from the River Niger after a boat that may have been carrying more than 200 passengers capsized.

The authorities have recommended measures including providing safer boats and life jackets, dredging waterways, deploying water guards at jetties and terminals, and ensuring boat operators are properly trained and licensed.

But many of these measures have not been fully implemented or properly enforced.

For millions of Nigerians, particularly in rural communities, rivers are an important means of transport. Many villages are located near waterways, while poor roads and a lack of bridges can make travel by land difficult.

Wooden boats are often used to transport people and goods, including to markets and neighbouring communities.

fullText:
